name: SpannerService.CreateSession
description: Creates a session, the handle a client uses to run reads, queries and transactions against one database; a session is meant to be reused for many consecutive transactions.

name: SpannerService.GetSession
description: Returns one session by name, mainly to check whether it is still alive; the call fails with NOT_FOUND if the session no longer exists.

name: SpannerService.ListSessions
description: Lists the sessions of a database, optionally narrowed by a filter on session labels and returned in pages with a page token.

name: ListSessions label filtering
description: A case-insensitive filter expression on the session list that matches sessions by label, such as having a given label key or a label value containing a given string.
notes: Applies AIP-160 label filters.

name: SpannerService.DeleteSession
description: Ends a session and releases the server resources it holds, which also cancels any operations still running in that session.

name: SpannerService.BatchCreateSessions
description: Creates many sessions for one database in a single request, which lets a client fill a session pool or cache up front.

name: SpannerService.Read
description: Reads rows from a table or index using key lookups and key range scans, as a key-value style alternative to SQL, and returns the whole result in one reply.

name: SpannerService.StreamingRead
description: Performs the same key-based read as Read but returns the rows as a stream of partial result sets, so large results can be consumed incrementally.

name: Streaming read resume after a row boundary
description: A resume token sent with the original read request lets a client continue a streamed read from the last token it received after an interruption, instead of starting over.
notes: Same transaction or read timestamp; rejects mismatched tokens.

name: SpannerService.ExecuteSql
description: Runs one SQL statement, a query or DML, and returns the complete result in a single reply together with result metadata and optional statistics.

name: SpannerService.ExecuteStreamingSql
description: Runs a SQL statement like ExecuteSql but returns the results as a stream of partial result sets, so large result sets can be read incrementally.

name: Streaming query resume after a row boundary
description: A resume token lets a client re-send the identical streamed query after a dropped connection and pick up after the last token it received instead of from the first row.
notes: Request/transaction-bound token; replays and verifies preceding rows.

name: Streaming query chunking of oversized rows
description: A streamed result can split one large value across several partial result sets, flagging the final value of a message as chunked so the client concatenates the pieces.
notes: PartialResultSet chunked_value; local response-size limits apply.

name: SpannerService.PartitionRead
description: Splits a read into partition tokens so separate workers can each run StreamingRead on a subset of the rows in parallel, all within one read-only transaction.
notes: Returns local tokens, one empty and one full partition; no real parallel partitioning.

name: SpannerService.PartitionQuery
description: Splits a SQL query into partition tokens that separate workers can each run with ExecuteStreamingSql to read a subset of the result in parallel in one read-only transaction.
notes: Returns local tokens, one empty and one full partition; no real parallel partitioning.

name: Single-use transaction selector
description: A transaction selector that runs one read or query in a temporary transaction created for that call, the most efficient choice for a single statement.

name: Existing transaction-ID selector
description: A transaction selector that runs a read or query inside a transaction that was already started, identified by the transaction ID returned when it began.

name: Inline begin selector
description: A transaction selector that starts a new transaction as part of a read or query request and returns its ID in the result metadata, saving a round trip.

name: Multiplexed session transactions
description: Runs transactions on a multiplexed session, a long-lived session that serves many concurrent transactions across gRPC channels without a session pool.
notes: Sessions remain transient across restart.

name: Multiplexed precommit-token retry handling
description: Read-write transactions on a multiplexed session carry a server-issued precommit token; if the response to the final request holds a new token, the client resends that request with it.
notes: Sessions remain transient across restart.

name: Directed-read replica routing
description: Lets read-only transactions and single reads name which replicas serve them, by including or excluding replicas by location and type; read-write transactions cannot use it.
notes: Options are validated but run on the same local engine.

name: Data Boost separate compute
description: Runs eligible read-only analytics queries and exports on separate serverless compute, so they do not use the provisioned instance's capacity or slow its transactional workload.
notes: Options are validated but run on the same local engine.

name: InstanceAdminService.ListInstanceConfigs
description: Lists the instance configurations available to a project, both Google-managed and user-managed; a configuration defines where an instance's data is replicated.
notes: Google's emulator exposes built-in config; LocalCloud also manages custom config metadata.

name: InstanceAdminService.GetInstanceConfig
description: Returns one instance configuration, including its replicas, leader options, state and etag.
notes: Google's emulator exposes built-in config; LocalCloud also manages custom config metadata.

name: InstanceAdminService.CreateInstanceConfig
description: Creates a user-managed instance configuration from a Google-managed base configuration, optionally adding replicas, and returns a long-running operation.

name: InstanceAdminService.UpdateInstanceConfig
description: Updates the display name or labels of a user-managed instance configuration, using an update mask and optionally an etag, as a long-running operation.

name: InstanceAdminService.DeleteInstanceConfig
description: Deletes a user-managed instance configuration that no instance uses, optionally guarded by an etag.

name: Custom instance-config metadata
description: A user-managed instance configuration builds on a Google-managed base configuration and records the replicas and regions that instances using it are placed in.
notes: Replicas and regions are metadata only.

name: Custom instance-config etag guards
description: An etag on an instance configuration provides optimistic concurrency control: when supplied, it must match the current configuration for an update or delete to go ahead.
notes: Updates/deletes validate supplied etags.

name: InstanceAdminService.ListInstances
description: Lists the instances of a project in pages, each with details such as its configuration, compute capacity, state and labels.

name: ListInstances field/label filtering
description: A case-insensitive filter expression that matches instances by name, display name or label, for example names containing a string or instances carrying a given label.
notes: Applies AIP-160 name, display_name and label filters.

name: InstanceAdminService.GetInstance
description: Returns the details of one instance, such as its configuration, compute capacity, state, edition and labels.

name: InstanceAdminService.CreateInstance
description: Creates an instance, the allocation of compute and storage resources that hosts databases, and returns a long-running operation that completes when it is ready to serve.

name: InstanceAdminService.UpdateInstance
description: Changes an instance, for example its display name, labels or compute capacity, using a field mask, and returns a long-running operation.

name: InstanceAdminService.DeleteInstance
description: Deletes an instance together with all of its databases and stops billing for its resources.

name: InstanceAdminService.MoveInstance
description: Moves an instance to a different instance configuration as a long-running operation, relocating its data to the new replicas without downtime.
notes: Updates instance-config metadata; no physical data movement.

name: InstanceAdminService.ListInstancePartitions
description: Lists all the instance partitions of an instance, the extra sets of resources that geo-partitioned data can be placed in.

name: InstanceAdminService.GetInstancePartition
description: Returns the details of one instance partition, such as its configuration, compute capacity and state.

name: InstanceAdminService.CreateInstancePartition
description: Creates an instance partition inside an instance, with its own configuration and compute capacity, and returns a long-running operation.

name: InstanceAdminService.UpdateInstancePartition
description: Changes an instance partition, for example its display name or compute capacity, using a field mask, and returns a long-running operation.

name: InstanceAdminService.DeleteInstancePartition
description: Deletes an instance partition that is not used by any database or backup and is not the default partition of its instance.

name: InstanceAdminService.ListInstancePartitionOperations
description: Lists the long-running operations on instance partitions of an instance, pending and recently finished, starting with the most recently started.

name: DatabaseAdminService.ListDatabases
description: Lists the databases that exist in an instance, returned in pages with a page token.

name: DatabaseAdminService.CreateDatabase
description: Creates a database in an instance, optionally with initial DDL statements, and returns a long-running operation that tracks its preparation for serving.

name: DatabaseAdminService.GetDatabase
description: Returns the state and configuration of one database, such as its dialect, encryption settings, version retention period and drop protection setting.

name: DatabaseAdminService.UpdateDatabase
description: Updates settings of an existing database, such as turning drop protection on or off, using an update mask and returning a long-running operation.

name: Enforced database drop protection
description: A database setting that, once enabled, makes deletion of the database fail until the setting is turned off, guarding against accidental deletion by authorized users.
notes: Prevents DropDatabase and cascading instance deletion.

name: DatabaseAdminService.DropDatabase
description: Deletes a database; completed backups of it are kept until their own expiration times.

name: DatabaseAdminService.CreateBackup
description: Starts creating a backup, a consistent copy of a database at a point in time that is stored separately and can later be restored, as a long-running operation.
notes: Local backup metadata or snapshots; snapshot/restore needs --data_dir; No CMEK; snapshots are full copies.

name: Historical backup version_time
description: A backup option that picks the past timestamp whose database contents the backup captures, an externally consistent copy at that time rather than at the request time.
notes: Snapshot captures schema/rows at a retained historical timestamp.

name: DatabaseAdminService.CopyBackup
description: Starts copying an existing backup into a new backup, possibly in another instance, as a long-running operation associated with the destination backup.
notes: Local backup metadata or snapshots; snapshot/restore needs --data_dir; No CMEK; snapshots are full copies.

name: DatabaseAdminService.GetBackup
description: Returns the metadata of one pending or completed backup, such as its state, size, expiration time and version time.
notes: Local backup metadata or snapshots; snapshot/restore needs --data_dir; No CMEK; snapshots are full copies.

name: DatabaseAdminService.ListBackups
description: Lists the pending and completed backups of an instance, newest first, optionally narrowed by a filter expression on fields such as name, state or create time.
notes: Local backup metadata or snapshots; snapshot/restore needs --data_dir; No CMEK; snapshots are full copies.

name: DatabaseAdminService.UpdateBackup
description: Changes settings of a pending or completed backup, such as its expiration time, using an update mask.
notes: Local backup metadata or snapshots; snapshot/restore needs --data_dir; No CMEK; snapshots are full copies.

name: DatabaseAdminService.DeleteBackup
description: Permanently deletes a pending or completed backup, after which it can no longer be used to restore a database.
notes: Local backup metadata or snapshots; snapshot/restore needs --data_dir; No CMEK; snapshots are full copies.

name: DatabaseAdminService.RestoreDatabase
description: Creates a new database from a completed backup as a long-running operation, in the same project and in an instance with the same configuration as the backup's instance.

name: DatabaseAdminService.ListBackupOperations
description: Lists the long-running operations on backups in an instance, such as creates and copies, covering pending operations and recently finished ones.
notes: Local backup metadata or snapshots; snapshot/restore needs --data_dir; No CMEK; snapshots are full copies.

name: DatabaseAdminService.ListDatabaseOperations
description: Lists the long-running operations on the databases of an instance, such as creation, restore and schema updates, both pending and recently finished.

name: InstanceAdminService.ListInstanceConfigOperations
description: Lists the long-running operations on user-managed instance configurations in a project, such as creation and update, starting with the most recently started.

name: OperationsService.ListOperations
description: Lists the long-running operations under a resource name that match a request filter, returned in pages, so callers can review pending and finished asynchronous work.

name: ListOperations filter expressions
description: A filter string on operation lists that narrows results by fields such as name, done state, error and metadata values, with conditions combined using AND, OR and NOT.
notes: AIP-160 filters; pagination tokens are bound to filters.

name: DatabaseAdminService.CreateBackupSchedule
description: Creates a schedule that automatically takes backups of a database on a cron-style timetable, with a retention period and either full or incremental backups.
notes: Local backup metadata or snapshots; snapshot/restore needs --data_dir; No CMEK; snapshots are full copies.

name: DatabaseAdminService.GetBackupSchedule
description: Returns one backup schedule by name, including its cron timetable, retention period and backup type.
notes: Local backup metadata or snapshots; snapshot/restore needs --data_dir; No CMEK; snapshots are full copies.

name: DatabaseAdminService.ListBackupSchedules
description: Lists all the backup schedules defined for a database.
notes: Local backup metadata or snapshots; snapshot/restore needs --data_dir; No CMEK; snapshots are full copies.

name: DatabaseAdminService.UpdateBackupSchedule
description: Changes selected settings of an existing backup schedule, such as its timetable or retention period, as chosen by an update mask.
notes: Local backup metadata or snapshots; snapshot/restore needs --data_dir; No CMEK; snapshots are full copies.

name: DatabaseAdminService.DeleteBackupSchedule
description: Deletes a backup schedule so that no further automatic backups are created from it.
notes: Local backup metadata or snapshots; snapshot/restore needs --data_dir; No CMEK; snapshots are full copies.

name: Scheduled full snapshot execution
description: A backup schedule of the full type creates a complete backup of the database each time its cron timetable fires and keeps each one for the schedule's retention period.
notes: Supported UTC cron schedules; persistent worker cursor.

name: Incremental backup chain metadata
description: Backups made by an incremental schedule belong to a chain with a shared chain ID, and each backup records the oldest version time of data the backup system keeps for it.
notes: Maintains chain fields.

name: Physically incremental backup storage
description: An incremental backup stores only the changes made since the previous backup in its chain, while the first backup of a chain is a full copy of the database.
notes: Every backup remains a full copy.

name: DatabaseAdminService.UpdateDatabaseDdl
description: Applies schema changes, such as creating, altering and dropping tables, columns and indexes, from a list of DDL statements and returns a long-running operation.

name: DatabaseAdminService.GetDatabaseDdl
description: Returns the current schema of a database as a list of formatted DDL statements; schema updates that are still pending are not included.

name: DatabaseAdminService.AddSplitPoints
description: Adds split points to chosen tables and indexes of a database, marking key boundaries where Spanner should divide data ahead of expected load.
notes: Stores and reports split metadata; does not physically pre-split storage.

name: OperationsService.GetOperation
description: Returns the latest state of a long-running operation by name, which clients poll to learn whether it is done and to read its result or error.

name: OperationsService.DeleteOperation
description: Tells the service that the client no longer needs a long-running operation's result and deletes its record, without cancelling the underlying work.

name: OperationsService.WaitOperation
description: Waits until a long-running operation is done or a timeout passes, then returns its latest state; it may return early, so callers should check the done flag.

name: OperationsService.CancelOperation
description: Starts a best-effort cancellation of a long-running operation; a cancelled operation is not deleted and ends with a CANCELLED error.
notes: Validates an already completed operation; no running work is canceled.

name: CREATE TABLE
description: Defines a new table with its columns, data types, constraints and primary key, and optionally interleaves it in a parent table.

name: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS
description: Creates a table only when no table of that name exists; if one does, the statement does nothing and raises no error.

name: Composite primary keys
description: A table's primary key can span several columns in a defined order; together they uniquely identify each row and determine the order in which rows are stored.

name: NOT NULL columns
description: A column annotation that makes the column required, so every row written must have a non-NULL value for it.

name: Hidden columns
description: A column marked HIDDEN is left out of SELECT * results but can still be selected by name; it mainly keeps TOKENLIST columns out of full-row queries.

name: Tables without an explicit primary key
description: A table created with no primary key columns, which can hold only a single row; this form exists only in GoogleSQL-dialect databases.
notes: Hidden system-assigned _rowid.

name: ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN
description: Adds a new column to an existing table, optionally with a default or stored generated value that is backfilled into the existing rows.
notes: Validated schema changes; multi-table RENAME TABLE is GoogleSQL-only.

name: ALTER TABLE DROP COLUMN
description: Removes a column, along with its data, from an existing table as a schema change.
notes: Validated schema changes; multi-table RENAME TABLE is GoogleSQL-only.

name: ALTER TABLE ALTER COLUMN
description: Changes an existing column, for example its data type, NOT NULL setting, default value, generated expression or column options.
notes: Validated schema changes; multi-table RENAME TABLE is GoogleSQL-only.

name: ALTER TABLE ADD CONSTRAINT
description: Adds a foreign key or CHECK constraint to an existing table, validating the data already in the table before the constraint takes effect.
notes: Validated schema changes; multi-table RENAME TABLE is GoogleSQL-only.

name: ALTER TABLE DROP CONSTRAINT
description: Removes a named constraint, such as a foreign key or CHECK constraint, from a table together with any index that backs it.
notes: Validated schema changes; multi-table RENAME TABLE is GoogleSQL-only.

name: ALTER TABLE RENAME TO
description: Renames an existing table, optionally adding a synonym so applications can keep using the old name while they move to the new one.
notes: Validated schema changes; multi-table RENAME TABLE is GoogleSQL-only.

name: RENAME TABLE
description: A GoogleSQL statement that renames one or several tables in a single operation, applying all the renames atomically.
notes: Validated schema changes; multi-table RENAME TABLE is GoogleSQL-only.

name: DROP TABLE
description: Permanently removes a table and its data, along with its foreign keys; the table cannot be recovered afterwards.

name: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS
description: Drops a table only if it exists; naming a table that does not exist has no effect and raises no error.

name: CREATE VIEW
description: Defines a named view stored in the schema as a SQL query whose results can be selected like a table, with a SQL SECURITY INVOKER or DEFINER setting.

name: CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW
description: Creates a view or, when one of that name already exists, replaces its definition; it is also how a view's security type is changed.

name: DROP VIEW
description: Removes a view from the schema without touching the tables that its query reads from.

name: SQL SECURITY INVOKER view evaluation
description: A view declared SQL SECURITY INVOKER runs its defining query as the user who queries it, so results reflect what that caller may see in the underlying tables.

name: SQL SECURITY INVOKER privilege checks
description: Under fine-grained access control, querying an INVOKER view needs SELECT on the view and on every table, column or view that it references.
notes: Checks underlying object privileges for role-restricted sessions, including PLAN.

name: SQL SECURITY DEFINER privilege checks
description: Under fine-grained access control, querying a DEFINER view needs only SELECT on the view itself, so a role can read a chosen subset of data without access to the underlying objects.
notes: Requires SELECT on the view instead of underlying objects.

name: CREATE SCHEMA
description: Creates a named schema, a namespace that groups tables, indexes, views and sequences, whose objects are then referred to by schema-qualified names.

name: DROP SCHEMA
description: Removes a named schema, the namespace that groups tables, views and other objects under qualified names.

name: Objects in named schemas
description: Tables, indexes, views and sequences can be created inside a named schema and are then referred to by their schema-qualified names.

name: CREATE SEQUENCE
description: Creates a sequence object that generates unique integers from an internal counter that is bit-reversed to spread inserts across the key space; usable as a column default.

name: ALTER SEQUENCE
description: Changes a sequence's options, such as its skipped value range or its counter, without affecting values the sequence has already generated.

name: DROP SEQUENCE
description: Removes a sequence object from the database schema so that it no longer generates values.

name: GET_NEXT_SEQUENCE_VALUE()
description: Takes a sequence and returns its next INT64 value; it can be used in a read-write transaction or as the default expression of a column.

name: GET_INTERNAL_SEQUENCE_STATE()
description: Returns a sequence's current internal counter before bit reversal as an INT64, useful for export and migration, or NULL if no value was ever generated.

name: Sequence counters across restart
description: A sequence's internal counter is stored durably, so after a restart the sequence carries on from where it left off and does not hand out earlier values again.
notes: Requires --data_dir; can skip up to 1,000 reserved values.

name: Sequence counters after backup restore
description: A backup captures a database's sequences together with its tables, so a database restored from it has those sequences available to generate values again.
notes: Restores the saved sequence allocation state.

name: CREATE FUNCTION
description: Defines a user-defined function in the schema, with typed parameters and a return type, that queries can then call by name.

name: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION
description: Defines a user-defined function, replacing the definition of any existing function of the same name; this is how function libraries are installed or updated.

name: Remote function execution against Cloud Run
description: A remote function is callable from SQL but runs in a Cloud Run or Cloud Run functions HTTPS endpoint, which receives batches of arguments as JSON and returns a reply for each call.
notes: Emulators return placeholders without production Cloud Run invocation.

name: GoogleSQL CREATE PLACEMENT
description: Defines a named placement tied to a user-created instance partition, with an optional default leader region, telling Spanner where rows tagged with it are stored.
notes: Adds lifecycle/partition-existence validation.

name: GoogleSQL ALTER PLACEMENT
description: Changes the options of an existing placement, the named location that maps rows to an instance partition, such as its default leader region.
notes: Validates placement options and referenced partitions.

name: GoogleSQL DROP PLACEMENT
description: Deletes a placement; it fails while rows of any placement table still use it, so those rows must first be moved to another placement or removed.
notes: Adds safe-drop checks.

name: PostgreSQL placement DDL
description: The PostgreSQL-dialect statements for geo-partitioning: CREATE PLACEMENT with a WITH clause of options, DROP PLACEMENT, and a PLACEMENT KEY column on tables.
notes: Translated placement lifecycle and placement-key DDL.

name: Placement-key mutation validation
description: Every row written to a placement table must carry a placement key value naming an existing placement or the value default, which decides the instance partition that stores the row.
notes: Checks placement keys; all rows remain local.

name: Placement preview DML restrictions
description: While geo-partitioning is in preview, DML on placement tables is restricted; for example, an INSERT or DELETE must be the only statement in its transaction.
notes: Optional --enforce_placement_dml_restrictions.

name: INFORMATION_SCHEMA.PLACEMENTS
description: A GoogleSQL schema view that lists each placement in the database by name, with a flag showing whether it is the default placement.
notes: Google's emulator v1.5.59 adds this too.

name: INFORMATION_SCHEMA.PLACEMENT_OPTIONS
description: A GoogleSQL schema view that lists the options set on each placement, such as instance_partition and default_leader, with each option's name, type and value.
notes: Google's emulator v1.5.59 adds this too.

name: INTERLEAVE IN PARENT
description: Declares a child table physically stored with its parent table's rows; the child's key must start with the parent's key and a parent row must exist, with ON DELETE CASCADE or NO ACTION.

name: INTERLEAVE IN
description: Co-locates a child table's rows with a parent table's rows like INTERLEAVE IN PARENT, but does not require that a parent row exist for each child row.

name: ALTER TABLE SET ON DELETE
description: Switches the delete behavior of an interleaved child table between CASCADE, which deletes child rows with their parent, and NO ACTION, which blocks deleting a parent that still has children.

name: ALTER TABLE SET INTERLEAVE IN
description: Changes an interleaved child table from INTERLEAVE IN PARENT to INTERLEAVE IN, keeping the co-location but dropping the requirement that each child row has a parent row.

name: GoogleSQL ROW DELETION POLICY DDL
description: Table clause ROW DELETION POLICY (OLDER_THAN(timestamp_column, INTERVAL n DAY)) that marks rows for automatic deletion once a timestamp column is older than the given number of days.
notes: Validates and stores policy.

name: PostgreSQL TTL INTERVAL DDL
description: PostgreSQL-dialect clause TTL INTERVAL 'n days' ON a TIMESTAMPTZ column, added in CREATE TABLE or ALTER TABLE, that deletes rows once the column is older than a whole number of days.
notes: Validates and stores policy.

name: TTL background deletion
description: A low-priority background process finds rows past their expiration and deletes them in batches, typically within a few days, without hiding expired rows from queries first.
notes: Default sweep interval 60 seconds; may contend with users.

name: TTL delete change-stream records
description: Change streams record TTL deletions as DELETE data change records whose transaction tag is RowDeletionPolicy and whose is_system_transaction field is true.
notes: RowDeletionPolicy tag and system-transaction flag.

name: exclude_ttl_deletes stream option effect
description: Change stream option that, when set to true, leaves out the records of rows removed by TTL, so only deletes issued by users appear in the stream.
notes: Filters sweeper deletes.

name: CREATE LOCALITY GROUP
description: Defines a locality group with a storage option of ssd or hdd and an optional ssd_to_hdd_spill_timespan after which data moves from SSD to HDD; columns and indexes can be assigned to it.
notes: DDL/catalog metadata only; no storage tiering.

name: ALTER LOCALITY GROUP
description: Changes the storage type, the SSD-to-HDD spill timespan, or both for an existing locality group; the built-in default group is named with backticks.
notes: DDL/catalog metadata only; no storage tiering.

name: DROP LOCALITY GROUP
description: Removes a locality group; it fails while the group still holds data, which must first be moved to another locality group.
notes: DDL/catalog metadata only; no storage tiering.

name: version_retention_period enforcement
description: Database option that sets how long Spanner keeps old versions of data and schema, which bounds how far back stale reads and point-in-time recovery can go.
notes: Enforced in historical reads, pruning and backup timestamps.

name: default_time_zone query effect
description: Database option that sets the IANA time zone Spanner uses for timestamp-to-date and civil time conversions when a query names no time zone.
notes: Applies to query/default/check/view evaluation.

name: default_sequence_kind option
description: Database option whose only valid value is bit_reversed_positive; sequences and identity columns that name no kind use it, producing positive INT64 values that are not sequential.
notes: Validated default sequence kind.

name: score_version metadata
description: Database option that sets the default version of the scoring algorithm behind the SCORE function in full-text search; a version in a query's SCORE options overrides it.
notes: Stored metadata; no production scoring engine.

name: witness_location physical effect
description: Database option naming the location of the witness replica, a replica that votes on writes to form a quorum but serves no reads.
notes: No witness placement.

name: read_lease_regions physical effect
description: Database option listing non-leader read-write or read-only regions that may serve strong reads from their own replicas, reducing strong read latency in those regions.
notes: No regional read leases.

name: per_placement_routing_metadata physical effect
description: Database option choosing where routing metadata lives for geo-partitioned data: with TRUE it sits in each placement's own partition, with FALSE it is centralized in the default partition.
notes: Metadata only.

name: columnar_policy physical effect
description: An option that configures the Spanner columnar engine, which builds a per-column storage layout in the background to speed up analytical queries on current operational data.
notes: No separate columnar storage engine.

name: CREATE QUEUE statement
description: Creates a queue, a table-like object that holds messages, with key columns, one Payload column, a primary key and options such as receive_mode, disable_send and disable_delivery.
notes: Not exposed in this LocalCloud baseline; v1.5.59 adds queues.

name: ALTER QUEUE statement
description: Changes an existing queue: sets options such as disable_send, disable_delivery and locality_group, changes ON DELETE or interleaving, and adds, drops or replaces its row deletion policy.
notes: Not exposed in this LocalCloud baseline.

name: DROP QUEUE statement
description: Deletes a queue; with IF EXISTS, naming a queue that does not exist is not an error.
notes: Not exposed in this LocalCloud baseline.

name: Queue RECEIVE execution
description: Calls the queue's RECEIVE table-valued function through ExecuteStreamingSQL to stream messages to a worker as a long-running query, each with a lease token and lease expiration time.
notes: Not exposed in this LocalCloud baseline.

name: Queue RENEWLEASE execution
description: Calls the queue's RENEWLEASE table-valued function with an array of lease tokens to extend the leases of messages being processed, so they are not redelivered on timeout.
notes: Not exposed in this LocalCloud baseline.

name: BOOL type
description: The Boolean type, holding TRUE or FALSE, or NULL when there is no value; used for logical conditions and flag columns.

name: INT64 type
description: The 64-bit signed integer type, ranging from -9223372036854775808 to 9223372036854775807, and the integer type of GoogleSQL.

name: FLOAT32 type
description: A single-precision approximate floating-point number type that follows IEEE-754 behaviour, including NaN and positive and negative infinity.

name: FLOAT64 type
description: A double-precision approximate floating-point number type that follows IEEE-754 behaviour, including NaN and positive and negative infinity.

name: GoogleSQL NUMERIC type
description: An exact decimal type with 38 digits of precision and 9 digits after the decimal point, suited to financial calculations.
notes: PostgreSQL NUMERIC cannot be a key column; persistence is tracked separately.

name: PostgreSQL NUMERIC type
description: A high-precision exact decimal type, also spelled decimal, that follows PostgreSQL semantics, such as NaN values being equal to each other and greater than every other value.
notes: PostgreSQL NUMERIC cannot be a key column; persistence is tracked separately.

name: GoogleSQL JSON type
description: A type for JSON documents stored in canonical form: whitespace is dropped, object members are ordered by key and array order is kept; values can be compared, grouped and sorted.

name: JSON null distinct from SQL NULL
description: A JSON null is an actual JSON value inside a document, while SQL NULL means no value at all; BOOL of a JSON null raises an error, but SQL NULL input gives SQL NULL.

name: GoogleSQL BOOL()
description: Converts a JSON boolean value to a SQL BOOL, and raises an error if the JSON value is not a boolean, including JSON null.

name: GoogleSQL BOOL_ARRAY()
description: Converts a JSON array of booleans to an ARRAY of BOOL values, and raises an error if the input is not an array or any element is not a boolean.

name: GoogleSQL FLOAT64()
description: Converts a JSON number to a FLOAT64; the wide_number_mode option chooses whether values that lose precision are rounded (the default) or raise an error.

name: GoogleSQL FLOAT64_ARRAY()
description: Converts a JSON array of numbers to an ARRAY of FLOAT64 values using the same wide_number_mode option, and raises an error for a non-array input or a non-number element.

name: GoogleSQL INT64()
description: Converts a JSON number with an integer value to an INT64; a value such as 10.0 is accepted, while fractional, out-of-range or non-numeric JSON raises an error.

name: GoogleSQL INT64_ARRAY()
description: Converts a JSON array of integer-valued numbers to an ARRAY of INT64 values, and raises an error if the input is not an array or any element is not an in-range integer.

name: GoogleSQL JSON_ARRAY()
description: Builds a JSON array from zero or more SQL values, turning SQL NULL into JSON null and returning an empty array when called with no arguments.

name: GoogleSQL JSON_ARRAY_APPEND()
description: Appends values to the end of the JSON arrays found at given JSONPaths and returns the updated JSON; SQL arrays are appended element by element unless append_each_element is FALSE.

name: GoogleSQL JSON_ARRAY_INSERT()
description: Inserts values into JSON arrays at the positions named by JSONPaths, padding with JSON null when the index is past the end, and returns the updated JSON.

name: GoogleSQL JSON_CONTAINS()
description: Returns TRUE when the first JSON value contains the second, such as an object holding all of another object's key-value pairs or an array holding all of another array's elements.

name: GoogleSQL JSON_KEYS()
description: Returns the unique keys of a JSON value as a sorted ARRAY of STRING; optional max_depth and mode arguments control how deep to look and whether keys inside arrays count.

name: GoogleSQL JSON_OBJECT()
description: Creates a JSON object from key-value pairs, given as alternating key and value arguments or as one array of keys and one array of values; with no arguments it returns an empty object.

name: GoogleSQL JSON_QUERY()
description: Extracts the value at a JSONPath from a JSON value or JSON-formatted string and returns it still in JSON form, so objects and arrays are kept; a missing path returns NULL.

name: GoogleSQL JSON_QUERY_ARRAY()
description: Extracts the JSON array at a JSONPath and returns its elements as an ARRAY of JSON values or JSON-formatted strings; returns NULL if the path is missing or does not hold an array.

name: GoogleSQL JSON_REMOVE()
description: Removes the values at one or more JSONPaths from a JSON value and returns the updated JSON; paths that do not exist are skipped.

name: GoogleSQL JSON_SET()
description: Inserts or replaces values at JSONPaths in a JSON value and returns the updated JSON; missing path elements are created unless create_if_missing is FALSE.

name: GoogleSQL JSON_STRIP_NULLS()
description: Removes JSON null values from objects and, by default, from arrays, with options to keep array nulls or drop emptied containers, and returns the cleaned JSON.

name: GoogleSQL JSON_TYPE()
description: Returns the type of the outermost value of a JSON input as a STRING, one of object, array, string, number, boolean or null.

name: GoogleSQL JSON_VALUE()
description: Extracts a scalar JSON value at a JSONPath and returns it as an unquoted STRING; objects, arrays, JSON null and missing paths return NULL.

name: GoogleSQL JSON_VALUE_ARRAY()
description: Extracts a JSON array of scalars at a JSONPath and returns it as an ARRAY of unquoted STRING values; returns NULL if the target is not an array of scalars.

name: GoogleSQL LAX_BOOL()
description: Converts a JSON boolean, a true or false string, or a number (zero is FALSE, anything else TRUE) to BOOL, returning NULL instead of an error for any other value.

name: GoogleSQL LAX_FLOAT64()
description: Converts a JSON number, or a JSON string holding a number such as NaN or Inf, to FLOAT64, returning NULL instead of an error when the value cannot be converted.

name: GoogleSQL LAX_INT64()
description: Converts a JSON boolean, number or numeric string to INT64, rounding fractions to the nearest integer and returning NULL instead of an error when conversion is impossible.

name: GoogleSQL LAX_STRING()
description: Converts a JSON string, number or boolean to a STRING, returning NULL instead of an error for JSON null, objects and arrays.

name: GoogleSQL PARSE_JSON()
description: Parses a JSON-formatted STRING into a JSON value; wide_number_mode decides whether numbers that lose precision raise an error (exact, the default) or are rounded.

name: GoogleSQL STRING()
description: Converts a JSON string value to a SQL STRING, and raises an error if the JSON value is not a string.

name: GoogleSQL STRING_ARRAY()
description: Converts a JSON array of strings to an ARRAY of STRING values, and raises an error if the input is not an array or any element is not a string.

name: GoogleSQL TO_JSON()
description: Converts a SQL value of any type to a JSON value; stringify_wide_numbers decides whether large integer and numeric values are written as JSON strings.

name: GoogleSQL TO_JSON_STRING()
description: Converts a JSON value to a STRING holding its JSON-formatted text, the reverse of parsing a string into JSON.

name: ARRAY type
description: An ordered list of zero or more elements that share one non-array type; an empty array and a NULL array are different values, and elements may be NULL.
notes: No nested ARRAY columns; supported scalar element types only.

name: ARRAY parameter binding
description: Passing a whole list of values as a single array-typed query parameter, which a statement can read as an array, for example with UNNEST or IN UNNEST.
notes: No nested ARRAY columns; supported scalar element types only.

name: ARRAY element validation
description: The rule that every element of an array must have the array's single element type, NULL elements are allowed, and an array cannot directly contain another array.
notes: No nested ARRAY columns; supported scalar element types only.

name: STRUCT query values
description: An ordered group of typed fields, each optionally named, created in a query with the STRUCT constructor or tuple syntax and read with dot notation.
notes: GoogleSQL only; STRUCT is not a table-column type.

name: ARRAY<STRUCT> query values
description: An array whose elements are structs, giving a list of records with named fields; built from an array of STRUCT values or an ARRAY subquery and expanded with UNNEST.
notes: GoogleSQL only; STRUCT is not a table-column type.

name: STRUCT query parameters
description: A STRUCT, or an array of STRUCT values, passed as a query parameter so a statement can read its fields or compare several columns against it at once.
notes: GoogleSQL only; STRUCT is not a table-column type.

name: CREATE PROTO BUNDLE
description: DDL statement that registers a list of Protocol Buffers message and enum types, taken from supplied descriptors, so columns and expressions can use them as PROTO and ENUM types.
notes: Query/in-memory support; persistent non-NULL PROTO/ENUM writes are unavailable.

name: ALTER PROTO BUNDLE
description: DDL statement that changes the registered proto bundle by inserting new message or enum types, updating existing ones, or deleting ones that are no longer needed.
notes: Query/in-memory support; persistent non-NULL PROTO/ENUM writes are unavailable.

name: DROP PROTO BUNDLE
description: DDL statement that deletes the database's proto bundle and with it the registered Protocol Buffers message and enum types.
notes: Query/in-memory support; persistent non-NULL PROTO/ENUM writes are unavailable.

name: PROTO type
description: A type for values that are Protocol Buffers messages, referred to by fully qualified message name and defined through the database's proto bundle.
notes: Query/in-memory support; persistent non-NULL PROTO/ENUM writes are unavailable.

name: ENUM type
description: A type for Protocol Buffers enum values, which map case-sensitive string names to integer constants and are referred to by fully qualified enum name from the proto bundle.
notes: Query/in-memory support; persistent non-NULL PROTO/ENUM writes are unavailable.

name: INTERVAL query type
description: A duration with year, month, day and time-of-day components down to nanoseconds, written as an INTERVAL expression and used in date and timestamp arithmetic.
notes: Queries only; INTERVAL columns are rejected.

name: STRING type
description: Variable-length Unicode character data stored as UTF-8; functions such as LENGTH and SUBSTR count characters rather than bytes.

name: BYTES type
description: Variable-length binary data that is a separate type from STRING; converting between the two needs an explicit cast, which applies UTF-8 encoding or decoding.

name: DATE type
description: A calendar date without time of day or time zone, from 0001-01-01 to 9999-12-31, written in the canonical YYYY-MM-DD form.

name: TIMESTAMP type
description: An absolute point in time with nanosecond precision, from 0001-01-01 to 9999-12-31 UTC; no time zone is stored with the value.

name: GoogleSQL UUID type
description: The GoogleSQL UUID type, a 128-bit universally unique identifier written as lowercase hexadecimal groups of 8-4-4-4-12 digits that can be cast to and from STRING and BYTES.
notes: Native typed keys, values, casts and public-API results.

name: PostgreSQL UUID type
description: The PostgreSQL-dialect uuid type for 128-bit universally unique identifiers, usable in primary keys, indexes and column defaults such as gen_random_uuid().
notes: Native typed keys, values, defaults and public-API results.

name: PostgreSQL gen_random_uuid()
description: PostgreSQL-dialect function that returns a randomly generated UUID as a uuid value, commonly used as a column DEFAULT to give each new row a unique key.
notes: Returns UUID; DEFAULT and RETURNING cases exist.

name: UUID rows across restart
description: UUID values written to table columns are stored durably with their rows, and later reads return the same identifiers exactly as they were written.
notes: Requires --data_dir.

name: GoogleSQL NEW_UUID()
description: Returns a new random UUID as a value of the UUID type, with 122 random bits laid out as 8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal digits following RFC 4122 section 4.4.

name: SELECT filtering
description: Narrows the rows a query returns with a WHERE condition, so only rows for which the boolean expression evaluates to TRUE appear in the result.

name: ORDER BY
description: Sorts the result rows by one or more expressions, ascending by default or descending with DESC; without it the order of returned rows is undefined.

name: LIMIT clause
description: Caps the number of rows a query returns at a non-negative integer count; LIMIT 0 returns no rows, and with a set operation the cap applies after the operation.

name: OFFSET clause
description: Skips a given number of rows before LIMIT starts returning rows, so paging needs an ORDER BY to give a repeatable result.

name: UNION ALL
description: Set operator that concatenates the rows of two queries and keeps duplicates, so a row found m times in one input and n times in the other appears m plus n times.

name: UNION DISTINCT
description: Set operator that combines the rows of two queries and removes duplicates, so each distinct row appears exactly once in the result.

name: INTERSECT
description: Set operator that returns only rows produced by both queries; DISTINCT returns each such row once, while ALL keeps the smaller of the two duplicate counts.

name: EXCEPT
description: Set operator that returns the rows of the first query that do not appear in the second; DISTINCT returns each row once, while ALL subtracts the duplicate counts.

name: SELECT * EXCEPT
description: Selects every column of a table or expression except the columns named in the EXCEPT list, and is distinct from the EXCEPT set operator.

name: UNNEST WITH OFFSET
description: Expands an array into one row per element and adds a column with each element's zero-based position in the array, named offset unless given an alias.

name: GoogleSQL ABS()
description: Returns the absolute value of a number with the same type as the input; raises an error for the most negative INT64, which has no positive counterpart.

name: GoogleSQL ACOS()
description: Returns the inverse cosine of a value in radians, between 0 and pi; raises an error if the input is outside the range from -1 to 1.

name: GoogleSQL ACOSH()
description: Returns the inverse hyperbolic cosine of a value; raises an error if the input is less than 1.

name: GoogleSQL ARRAY_CONCAT()
description: Joins one or more arrays of the same element type into a single array in argument order; returns NULL if any input array is NULL.

name: GoogleSQL ARRAY_FILTER()
description: Returns an array holding only the elements for which a lambda condition is TRUE, in original order; the lambda may also receive the zero-based index, and FALSE or NULL drops the element.

name: GoogleSQL ARRAY_FIRST()
description: Returns the first element of an array, and raises an error if the array is empty.

name: GoogleSQL ARRAY_INCLUDES()
description: Returns TRUE if any element of an array equals a given search value, or in its lambda form satisfies a condition, and FALSE otherwise.

name: GoogleSQL ARRAY_INCLUDES_ALL()
description: Returns TRUE only if every element of the second array is also found in the first array.

name: GoogleSQL ARRAY_INCLUDES_ANY()
description: Returns TRUE if at least one element of the second array is also found in the first array.

name: GoogleSQL ARRAY_IS_DISTINCT()
description: Returns TRUE if an array has no repeated elements; NULL elements count as equal to each other, and an empty array is distinct.

name: GoogleSQL ARRAY_LAST()
description: Returns the last element of an array, and raises an error if the array is empty.

name: GoogleSQL ARRAY_LENGTH()
description: Returns the number of elements in an array as an INT64, counting NULL elements; an empty array gives 0 and a NULL array gives NULL.

name: GoogleSQL ARRAY_MAX()
description: Returns the largest non-NULL element of an array, or NULL if the array is empty or contains only NULL elements.

name: GoogleSQL ARRAY_MIN()
description: Returns the smallest non-NULL element of an array, or NULL if the array is empty or contains only NULL elements.

name: GoogleSQL ARRAY_REVERSE()
description: Returns an array containing the same elements as the input in reverse order.

name: GoogleSQL ARRAY_SLICE()
description: Returns the elements from a start offset through an end offset, both inclusive and zero-based; negative offsets count back from the end and out-of-range offsets are clamped.

name: GoogleSQL ARRAY_TO_STRING()
description: Joins the elements of a STRING or BYTES array into one value separated by a delimiter, leaving out NULL elements unless a replacement text is given.

name: GoogleSQL ARRAY_TRANSFORM()
description: Returns an array of the same length where each element is replaced by the result of a lambda expression applied to it, optionally using the element's zero-based index.

name: GoogleSQL ASIN()
description: Returns the inverse sine of a value in radians, between minus pi over 2 and pi over 2; raises an error if the input is outside the range from -1 to 1.

name: GoogleSQL ASINH()
description: Returns the inverse hyperbolic sine of a value, which is defined for every real number.

name: GoogleSQL ATAN()
description: Returns the inverse tangent of a value in radians, between minus pi over 2 and pi over 2.

name: GoogleSQL ATAN2()
description: Returns the inverse tangent of X divided by Y in radians, using the signs of both arguments to choose the quadrant, so the result lies between minus pi and pi.

name: GoogleSQL ATANH()
description: Returns the inverse hyperbolic tangent of a value; raises an error if the input is below -1 or above 1.

name: GoogleSQL BIT_COUNT()
description: Returns the number of bits set to 1 in an integer or BYTES value; for a negative integer it counts the bits of its two's complement form.

name: GoogleSQL CEIL()
description: Returns the smallest whole number that is not less than the input, so 2.3 becomes 3.0 and -2.3 becomes -2.0; CEILING is a synonym.

name: GoogleSQL COALESCE()
description: Returns the first argument that is not NULL, or NULL if all are NULL; arguments are evaluated left to right and must share a common supertype.

name: GoogleSQL COS()
description: Returns the cosine of an angle given in radians, as a floating-point value between -1 and 1.

name: GoogleSQL COSH()
description: Returns the hyperbolic cosine of a value, and raises an error if the result overflows.

name: GoogleSQL DIV()
description: Divides the first integer by the second and returns the whole-number quotient truncated toward zero, so DIV(20, 3) is 6 and DIV(12, -7) is -1; dividing by zero raises an error.

name: GoogleSQL ERROR()
description: Raises an error with the given message string whenever it is evaluated, which lets a conditional expression stop a query on invalid data.

name: GoogleSQL EXP()
description: Returns e raised to the power of the input; the result underflows to 0 for very negative inputs and raises an error on overflow.

name: GoogleSQL FARM_FINGERPRINT()
description: Computes the FarmHash fingerprint of a STRING or BYTES input and returns it as an INT64 that never changes for the same input.

name: GoogleSQL FLOAT32()
description: Converts a JSON number to a FLOAT32; the wide_number_mode option chooses whether values that lose precision are rounded or raise an error.

name: GoogleSQL FLOAT32_ARRAY()
description: Converts a JSON array of numbers to an ARRAY of FLOAT32 values, and raises an error for a non-array input or an element that is not a number.

name: GoogleSQL FLOOR()
description: Returns the largest whole number that is not greater than the input, so 2.3 becomes 2.0 and -2.3 becomes -3.0.

name: GoogleSQL GENERATE_ARRAY()
description: Creates an array of numbers from a start value to an end value, both inclusive, stepping by 1 or a given step; the array is empty when the start is already past the end, and a step of 0 is an error.

name: GoogleSQL GENERATE_UUID()
description: Returns a random version 4 UUID as a lowercase STRING in 8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal form, as described in RFC 4122 section 4.4.

name: GoogleSQL GREATEST()
description: Returns the largest of its arguments by ordering rules; the result is NULL if any argument is NULL, and NaN if any floating-point argument is NaN.

name: GoogleSQL IEEE_DIVIDE()
description: Divides X by Y following IEEE 754 rules, so a zero divisor gives positive or negative infinity and 0 divided by 0 gives NaN instead of an error.

name: GoogleSQL IF()
description: Returns the second argument when the condition is TRUE and the third when it is FALSE or NULL, evaluating only the result it returns.

name: GoogleSQL IFNULL()
description: Returns the first argument unless it is NULL, in which case it returns the second; it is the two-argument form of COALESCE.

name: GoogleSQL IS_INF()
description: Returns TRUE if a floating-point value is positive or negative infinity and FALSE otherwise.

name: GoogleSQL IS_NAN()
description: Returns TRUE if a floating-point value is NaN, meaning not a number, and FALSE otherwise.

name: GoogleSQL JUSTIFY_DAYS()
description: Normalizes the day part of an INTERVAL to between -29 and 29 by carrying each 30 days into the month part, so 31 days becomes 1 month and 1 day.

name: GoogleSQL JUSTIFY_HOURS()
description: Normalizes the time part of an INTERVAL to less than a day in either direction by carrying whole 24-hour blocks into the day part, so 47 hours becomes 1 day and 23 hours.

name: GoogleSQL LEAST()
description: Returns the smallest of its arguments by ordering rules; the result is NULL if any argument is NULL, and NaN if any floating-point argument is NaN.

name: GoogleSQL LN()
description: Returns the natural logarithm of a number, and raises an error if the input is zero or negative.

name: GoogleSQL LOG()
description: Returns the natural logarithm of X, or the logarithm of X in base Y when a second argument is given; raises an error for a non-positive X, or a base that is not positive or equals 1.

name: GoogleSQL LOG10()
description: Returns the base-10 logarithm of a number, and raises an error if the input is zero or negative.

name: GoogleSQL MOD()
description: Returns the remainder of dividing the first integer by the second; the result takes the sign of the first argument, and dividing by zero raises an error.

name: GoogleSQL NULLIF()
description: Returns NULL when the two arguments are equal and otherwise returns the first argument, which is handy for turning a placeholder value into NULL.

name: GoogleSQL POW()
description: Returns X raised to the power Y; POWER is a synonym, and the call raises an error for zero to a negative power or a negative base with a non-integer exponent.

name: GoogleSQL ROUND()
description: Rounds X to the nearest whole number, or to a given number of decimal places, where a negative count rounds digits left of the decimal point; halfway values round away from zero.

name: GoogleSQL SAFE_ADD()
description: Adds two numbers like the plus operator but returns NULL instead of raising an overflow error.

name: GoogleSQL SAFE_DIVIDE()
description: Divides X by Y like the division operator but returns NULL instead of raising an error, for example when Y is zero.

name: GoogleSQL SAFE_MULTIPLY()
description: Multiplies two numbers like the multiplication operator but returns NULL instead of raising an overflow error.

name: GoogleSQL SAFE_NEGATE()
description: Negates a number like the unary minus operator but returns NULL instead of an overflow error, as happens for the most negative INT64.

name: GoogleSQL SAFE_SUBTRACT()
description: Subtracts the second number from the first like the minus operator but returns NULL instead of raising an overflow error.

name: GoogleSQL SAFE_TO_JSON()
description: Converts a SQL value to JSON like TO_JSON, but writes JSON null for any field it cannot convert instead of raising an error.

name: GoogleSQL SHA1()
description: Computes the SHA-1 hash of a STRING or BYTES input and returns the 20-byte digest as BYTES; it has known weaknesses and is not meant for new security designs.

name: GoogleSQL SHA256()
description: Computes the SHA-256 hash of a STRING or BYTES input and returns the 32-byte digest as BYTES.

name: GoogleSQL SHA512()
description: Computes the SHA-512 hash of a STRING or BYTES input and returns the 64-byte digest as BYTES, twice the size of a SHA-256 digest.

name: GoogleSQL SIGN()
description: Returns -1, 0 or +1 according to whether the input is negative, zero or positive, and NaN for a NaN input.

name: GoogleSQL SIN()
description: Returns the sine of an angle given in radians, as a floating-point value between -1 and 1.

name: GoogleSQL SINH()
description: Returns the hyperbolic sine of a value, and raises an error if the result overflows.

name: GoogleSQL SQRT()
description: Returns the square root of a number, and raises an error if the input is negative.

name: GoogleSQL TAN()
description: Returns the tangent of an angle given in radians, and raises an error if the result overflows.

name: GoogleSQL TANH()
description: Returns the hyperbolic tangent of a value, which always lies between -1 and 1.

name: GoogleSQL TRUNC()
description: Rounds a number toward zero to a whole number, or to a given number of decimal places, so TRUNC(-2.8) is -2.0 and the result never exceeds the input in absolute value.

name: GoogleSQL NET.IP_FROM_STRING()
description: Converts a text IPv4 or IPv6 address to its network-byte-order BYTES form of 4 or 16 bytes; invalid text, including CIDR notation, raises an error.

name: GoogleSQL NET.SAFE_IP_FROM_STRING()
description: Converts a text IPv4 or IPv6 address to network-byte-order BYTES like NET.IP_FROM_STRING, but returns NULL instead of an error when the text is not a valid address.

name: GoogleSQL NET.IP_TO_STRING()
description: Converts a 4-byte or 16-byte network-byte-order BYTES value to its IPv4 or IPv6 text form; any other length raises an error.

name: GoogleSQL NET.IP_NET_MASK()
description: Builds a network mask as BYTES of 4 or 16 bytes whose first prefix-length bits are 1 and remaining bits are 0, from a byte count and a prefix length.

name: GoogleSQL NET.IP_TRUNC()
description: Keeps the first prefix-length bits of an IP address in BYTES form and sets all remaining bits to zero, returning the network address at the same byte length.

name: GoogleSQL NET.IPV4_FROM_INT64()
description: Converts an INT64 integer to a 4-byte network-byte-order IPv4 address in BYTES; values outside -0x80000000 through 0xFFFFFFFF raise an error.

name: GoogleSQL NET.IPV4_TO_INT64()
description: Converts a 4-byte network-byte-order IPv4 address in BYTES to an INT64 between 0 and 0xFFFFFFFF; input of any other length raises an error.

name: GoogleSQL NET.HOST()
description: Extracts the host from a URL string using a best-effort RFC 3986 parse, without changing its case; returns NULL if the host cannot be parsed.

name: GoogleSQL NET.PUBLIC_SUFFIX()
description: Returns the public suffix of the host in a URL or host string, such as com or co.uk, based on the ICANN list; returns NULL if no suffix can be found.

name: GoogleSQL NET.REG_DOMAIN()
description: Returns the registered domain of a URL or host string, which is its public suffix plus the one label before it; returns NULL if the host is only a suffix or cannot be parsed.

name: INNER JOIN
description: Combines rows from two inputs and keeps only the pairs that satisfy the ON or USING condition; rows with no match on the other side are left out of the result.

name: LEFT JOIN
description: Keeps every row from the left input and adds matching right-input rows, filling the right-side columns with NULL for left rows that have no match.

name: RIGHT JOIN
description: Keeps every row from the right input and adds matching left-input rows, filling the left-side columns with NULL for right rows that have no match.

name: FULL JOIN
description: Keeps every row from both inputs: matching pairs are combined, and rows without a match on either side are returned with NULL in the other side's columns.

name: CROSS JOIN
description: Returns every combination of one left-input row with one right-input row, so the result has M times N rows; it takes no ON or USING condition.

name: Join against UNNEST
description: Joins each row to the elements of an array expression, where UNNEST turns the array into one row per element; an empty or NULL array contributes no rows to a cross or inner join.

name: Scalar subqueries
description: A parenthesized query used as a single value; it must return one column and at most one row, giving NULL when it returns no rows and an error when it returns more than one row.

name: ARRAY subqueries
description: Written as ARRAY followed by a parenthesized query that selects one column; it gathers all returned rows into one array value, and an empty result gives an empty array.

name: IN subqueries
description: Checks whether a value is found among the rows of a single-column subquery, written as an expression, IN, and a parenthesized query; NOT IN negates the check.

name: EXISTS subqueries
description: Evaluates to TRUE when the parenthesized query returns at least one row and FALSE when it returns none; the columns and values the subquery selects do not affect the result.

name: Correlated subqueries
description: A subquery that refers to columns of the enclosing query, so it is evaluated against each outer row, for example to look up related rows with EXISTS or a scalar lookup.

name: GoogleSQL named parameters
description: Placeholders written as an at sign followed by a name, such as @user_id, whose values are bound separately from the SQL text when the statement runs.

name: PostgreSQL positional parameters
description: Placeholders in PostgreSQL-dialect statements written as a dollar sign and a number, such as $1 and $2, which stand for values that are supplied separately from the SQL text.

name: Untyped parameter inference
description: When a parameter's type is not given in the request's param_types, Spanner infers its SQL type from the supplied value and from how the parameter is used in the statement.

name: Missing-parameter validation
description: Running a statement that refers to a parameter with no supplied value is an error, so every placeholder in the SQL text needs a matching entry in the request's params.

name: FORCE_INDEX validation
description: Table hint that names the index a query must read instead of letting the optimizer choose; _BASE_TABLE forces the base table, and naming an index that does not exist raises an error.
notes: Checks index existence; PostgreSQL unknown indexes are ignored.

name: LOCK_SCANNED_RANGES=exclusive lock effect
description: Statement hint that makes a statement take exclusive instead of shared locks on the ranges it scans, reducing aborts and retries when many transactions contend for the same rows.
notes: Acquires exclusive locks.

name: OPTIMIZER_VERSION query hint
description: Statement hint on a query that pins the query optimizer version used to compile it, as a version number, latest_version or default_version, overriding client and database settings.
notes: Accepted and validated; no production optimizer selection.

name: OPTIMIZER_VERSION DML hint
description: Statement hint placed before an INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE statement that selects the query optimizer version used to compile that DML statement, overriding client and database settings.
notes: Accepted and validated; no production optimizer selection.

name: OPTIMIZER_STATISTICS_PACKAGE hint effect
description: Statement hint that chooses which optimizer statistics package, named in INFORMATION_SCHEMA.SPANNER_STATISTICS or set to latest, the optimizer uses when planning the statement.
notes: Does not use a production statistics package.

name: JOIN_METHOD hint effect
description: Join hint that selects the physical join algorithm, such as HASH_JOIN, APPLY_JOIN, MERGE_JOIN or PUSH_BROADCAST_HASH_JOIN, instead of letting the optimizer decide.
notes: Validated but does not select a production join implementation.

name: INDEX_STRATEGY hint effect
description: Table hint INDEX_STRATEGY=FORCE_INDEX_UNION that reads from two or more indexes and unions their results, which suits WHERE clauses that combine OR conditions on different columns.
notes: Validated without the physical optimization.

name: GROUP_METHOD hint effect
description: Hint on GROUP BY that picks the aggregation strategy: HASH_GROUP builds an in-memory hash table of groups, while STREAM_GROUP aggregates already sorted input without buffering groups.
notes: Validated without the physical optimization.

name: PLAN query-plan tree
description: Query mode that returns only the query plan, a tree of operator nodes describing how the statement would run, with no result rows and no execution statistics.
notes: Analyzes without executing; local tree shape.

name: PROFILE query-plan tree
description: Query mode that runs the statement and returns its plan tree with execution statistics on each operator node, along with the result rows; it adds overhead compared with other modes.
notes: Local engine plan and timing.

name: PROFILE table-scan statistics
description: Operator-level figures that PROFILE mode attaches to the table and index scan nodes of a plan, such as how many rows each scan read, showing how much data the query touched.
notes: Measured local scans; DML reports root only.

name: WITH_STATS execution statistics
description: Query mode that returns the result rows plus overall execution statistics such as rows returned, elapsed time and CPU time, but no query plan and no per-operator statistics.
notes: Local rows, time and CPU counters.

name: WITH_PLAN_AND_STATS response
description: Query mode that returns the result rows together with the query plan and overall execution statistics, without the per-operator statistics that PROFILE adds.
notes: Local plan plus execution statistics.

name: GoogleSQL TABLESAMPLE BERNOULLI
description: Sampling method that includes each row of a table independently with the given percent probability, so the sample holds about that share of the rows and its size varies between runs.

name: GoogleSQL TABLESAMPLE RESERVOIR
description: Sampling method that takes a sample size in rows and returns exactly that many rows, or the whole input when it has fewer, with every sample of that size equally likely.

name: GoogleSQL TABLESAMPLE REPEATABLE
description: Optional clause with an integer repeat argument so that sampling the same data with the same argument selects the same sample of rows, rather than a new random sample each run.
notes: Seeded local sampling; not PostgreSQL REPEATABLE.

name: GoogleSQL ANY_VALUE()
description: Aggregate that returns the expression's value from some row of the group; which row is chosen is not specified, and it returns NULL when the group has no rows.

name: GoogleSQL ARRAY_AGG()
description: Aggregate that collects an expression's values from the rows of a group into one array; it accepts DISTINCT, IGNORE NULLS or RESPECT NULLS, ORDER BY and LIMIT inside the call.

name: GoogleSQL ARRAY_CONCAT_AGG()
description: Aggregate that joins the array values of all rows in a group into one longer array; NULL arrays are skipped and the result is NULL when there is no non-NULL array.

name: GoogleSQL AVG()
description: Aggregate that returns the average of the non-NULL numeric values in a group, as FLOAT64 for integer and float inputs, or NULL when the group has no non-NULL values.

name: GoogleSQL BIT_AND()
description: Aggregate that returns the bitwise AND of the INT64 values in a group, keeping only the bits that are set in every value.

name: GoogleSQL BIT_OR()
description: Aggregate that returns the bitwise OR of the INT64 values in a group, setting every bit that is set in at least one value.

name: GoogleSQL BIT_XOR()
description: Aggregate that returns the bitwise exclusive OR of the INT64 values in a group, setting each bit that is set in an odd number of values.

name: GoogleSQL COUNT()
description: Aggregate that returns an INT64 row count: COUNT(*) counts all rows in the group, while COUNT of an expression counts only rows where it is not NULL, optionally with DISTINCT.

name: GoogleSQL COUNTIF()
description: Aggregate that returns an INT64 count of the rows in a group for which a BOOL expression is TRUE; rows where it is FALSE or NULL are not counted.

name: GoogleSQL LOGICAL_AND()
description: Aggregate over BOOL values that returns TRUE only if every non-NULL value in the group is TRUE, and NULL when the group has no non-NULL values.

name: GoogleSQL LOGICAL_OR()
description: Aggregate over BOOL values that returns TRUE if at least one non-NULL value in the group is TRUE, and NULL when the group has no non-NULL values.

name: GoogleSQL MAX()
description: Aggregate that returns the largest non-NULL value of an orderable expression in a group, or NULL for an empty or all-NULL group; the result is NaN if any input is NaN.

name: GoogleSQL MIN()
description: Aggregate that returns the smallest non-NULL value of an orderable expression in a group, or NULL for an empty or all-NULL group; the result is NaN if any input is NaN.

name: GoogleSQL STDDEV()
description: Returns the sample standard deviation of the numeric values in a group, as FLOAT64; this short name behaves exactly like STDDEV_SAMP.

name: GoogleSQL STDDEV_SAMP()
description: Aggregate returning the sample (unbiased, n minus 1) standard deviation of a group's numeric values as FLOAT64; NULL inputs are ignored and fewer than two values give NULL.

name: GoogleSQL STRING_AGG()
description: Aggregate that concatenates the non-NULL STRING or BYTES values of a group into one value, with an optional delimiter, and optional DISTINCT, ORDER BY and LIMIT inside the call.

name: GoogleSQL SUM()
description: Aggregate that adds up the non-NULL numeric values in a group and returns NULL when there are none; an integer sum that overflows INT64 raises an error.

name: GoogleSQL VAR_SAMP()
description: Aggregate returning the sample (unbiased, n minus 1) variance of a group's numeric values as FLOAT64, the square of the sample standard deviation; fewer than two non-NULL values give NULL.

name: GoogleSQL VARIANCE()
description: Returns the sample variance of the numeric values in a group, as FLOAT64, measuring how far values spread from their mean; this short name behaves exactly like VAR_SAMP.

name: GoogleSQL BYTE_LENGTH()
description: Returns the number of bytes in a STRING or BYTES value as INT64, so a multibyte UTF-8 character counts as more than one.

name: GoogleSQL CHAR_LENGTH()
description: Returns the number of characters in a STRING as INT64, counting each character once however many bytes its UTF-8 encoding takes.

name: GoogleSQL CODE_POINTS_TO_BYTES()
description: Converts an array of INT64 values from 0 to 255 into a BYTES value with one byte per element; it reverses TO_CODE_POINTS applied to BYTES.

name: GoogleSQL CODE_POINTS_TO_STRING()
description: Converts an array of INT64 Unicode code points into a STRING; it reverses TO_CODE_POINTS applied to a STRING, and a NULL element makes the result NULL.

name: GoogleSQL CONCAT()
description: Joins one or more STRING or BYTES values, all of the same type, into a single value; the result is NULL if any argument is NULL.

name: GoogleSQL ENDS_WITH()
description: Returns TRUE if a STRING or BYTES value ends with the given suffix and FALSE otherwise; both arguments must have the same type.

name: GoogleSQL FORMAT()
description: Builds a STRING from a format string and a list of values, in the style of C printf, with specifiers such as %d for integers, %s for strings and %t for any value as text.

name: GoogleSQL FROM_BASE32()
description: Decodes a base32-encoded STRING into BYTES; it reverses TO_BASE32.

name: GoogleSQL FROM_BASE64()
description: Decodes a standard base64 STRING, using the characters A-Z, a-z, 0-9, plus, slash and equals, into BYTES; it reverses TO_BASE64.

name: GoogleSQL FROM_HEX()
description: Decodes a hexadecimal STRING, in upper or lower case, into BYTES; an odd number of digits is read as if it had a leading zero, and other characters raise an error.

name: GoogleSQL LENGTH()
description: Returns the length of a value as INT64: the number of characters for a STRING, but the number of bytes for a BYTES value.

name: GoogleSQL LOWER()
description: Converts a STRING to lowercase using Unicode character mappings without language-specific rules; for BYTES only the ASCII letters are lowercased.

name: GoogleSQL LPAD()
description: Pads the start of a STRING or BYTES value with a repeated pattern, a space by default, until it reaches the requested length; a longer value is cut down to that length.

name: GoogleSQL LTRIM()
description: Removes characters from the start of a STRING or BYTES value only: whitespace by default for a STRING, or any characters found in a given set.

name: GoogleSQL NORMALIZE()
description: Converts a STRING to a Unicode normalization form, NFC by default or NFD, NFKC or NFKD, so equivalent characters get one representation; letter case is kept.

name: GoogleSQL NORMALIZE_AND_CASEFOLD()
description: Normalizes a STRING to a Unicode form, as NORMALIZE does, and then case-folds it, so strings can be compared regardless of letter case or equivalent character encodings.

name: GoogleSQL REGEXP_CONTAINS()
description: Returns TRUE if any part of a STRING or BYTES value matches an RE2 regular expression; use anchors to require a match of the whole value.

name: GoogleSQL REGEXP_EXTRACT()
description: Returns the first substring that matches an RE2 regular expression, or the text captured by its single capturing group, and NULL when nothing matches.

name: GoogleSQL REGEXP_EXTRACT_ALL()
description: Returns an array of every non-overlapping substring matching an RE2 regular expression, or of its capturing group's text for each match, and an empty array when nothing matches.

name: GoogleSQL REGEXP_REPLACE()
description: Replaces every non-overlapping match of an RE2 regular expression in a STRING or BYTES value with a replacement, which can refer to captured groups.

name: GoogleSQL REPEAT()
description: Returns a STRING or BYTES value repeated a given number of times; a negative count raises an error and a NULL argument gives NULL.

name: GoogleSQL REPLACE()
description: Replaces every occurrence of a search value inside a STRING or BYTES value with another value and returns the changed copy.

name: GoogleSQL REVERSE()
description: Returns a STRING with its characters in reverse order, or a BYTES value with its bytes in reverse order.

name: GoogleSQL RPAD()
description: Pads the end of a STRING or BYTES value with a repeated pattern, a space by default, until it reaches the requested length; a longer value is cut down to that length.

name: GoogleSQL RTRIM()
description: Removes characters from the end of a STRING or BYTES value only: whitespace by default for a STRING, or any characters found in a given set.

name: GoogleSQL SAFE_CONVERT_BYTES_TO_STRING()
description: Converts a BYTES value to a STRING and replaces any invalid UTF-8 sequence with the Unicode replacement character U+FFFD instead of raising an error.

name: GoogleSQL SOUNDEX()
description: Returns the Soundex phonetic code of a STRING, a letter followed by three digits, so words that sound alike get the same code; non-Latin characters are ignored.

name: GoogleSQL SPLIT()
description: Splits a STRING, on a comma by default, or a BYTES value on a required delimiter, into an array of the pieces; the delimiter is matched literally, not as a pattern.

name: GoogleSQL SPLIT_SUBSTR()
description: Splits a STRING on a delimiter and returns the run of consecutive pieces from a start position for an optional count, rejoined with the delimiter; a negative start counts from the end.

name: GoogleSQL STARTS_WITH()
description: Returns TRUE if a STRING or BYTES value begins with the given prefix and FALSE otherwise; both arguments must have the same type.

name: GoogleSQL STRPOS()
description: Returns the 1-based position of the first occurrence of a substring within a STRING or BYTES value, or 0 when the substring is not found.

name: GoogleSQL SUBSTR()
description: Returns part of a STRING or BYTES value starting at a 1-based position for an optional length; a negative position counts back from the end of the value.

name: GoogleSQL TO_BASE32()
description: Encodes a BYTES value as a base32 STRING, padded with equals signs; it reverses FROM_BASE32.

name: GoogleSQL TO_BASE64()
description: Encodes a BYTES value as a standard base64 STRING with padding; it reverses FROM_BASE64, and URL-safe output needs plus and slash replaced.

name: GoogleSQL TO_CODE_POINTS()
description: Converts a STRING into an array of its Unicode code points, or a BYTES value into an array of its byte values from 0 to 255, as INT64 elements.

name: GoogleSQL TO_HEX()
description: Converts a BYTES value to a lowercase hexadecimal STRING with two digits per byte; it reverses FROM_HEX.

name: GoogleSQL TRIM()
description: Removes characters from both ends of a STRING or BYTES value: whitespace by default for a STRING, or any characters found in a given set.

name: GoogleSQL UPPER()
description: Converts a STRING to uppercase using Unicode character mappings without language-specific rules; for BYTES only the ASCII letters are uppercased.

name: GoogleSQL ZSTD_COMPRESS()
description: Compresses a STRING or BYTES value into BYTES with the Zstandard algorithm; an optional level argument trades compression speed for a smaller result.

name: GoogleSQL ZSTD_DECOMPRESS_TO_BYTES()
description: Decompresses Zstandard-compressed BYTES back into BYTES; an optional size_limit caps the decompressed size, and a result larger than the limit raises an error.

name: GoogleSQL ZSTD_DECOMPRESS_TO_STRING()
description: Decompresses Zstandard-compressed BYTES into a STRING, for data that was compressed from text; an optional size_limit caps the output size and exceeding it raises an error.

name: GoogleSQL LCASE()
