description: A synonym of LOWER: returns a STRING in lowercase, or a BYTES value with only its ASCII letters lowercased.

name: GoogleSQL UCASE()
description: A synonym of UPPER: returns a STRING in uppercase, or a BYTES value with only its ASCII letters uppercased.

name: GoogleSQL CURRENT_DATE()
description: Returns today's date as a DATE, optionally for a given time zone; every call within one statement returns the same value.

name: GoogleSQL CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()
description: Returns the current date and time as a TIMESTAMP; every call within one statement returns the same value, and the parentheses may be omitted.

name: GoogleSQL DATE()
description: Constructs a DATE from INT64 year, month and day arguments, or extracts the date part of a TIMESTAMP as seen in an optional time zone.

name: GoogleSQL DATE_ADD()
description: Adds a number of DAY, WEEK, MONTH, QUARTER or YEAR units to a DATE and returns the new DATE; month arithmetic that lands past a short month's end gives its last day.

name: GoogleSQL DATE_DIFF()
description: Returns, as INT64, the number of DAY, WEEK, MONTH, QUARTER or YEAR boundaries between an end date and a start date, zero or negative when the end date is earlier.

name: GoogleSQL DATE_FROM_UNIX_DATE()
description: Converts an INT64 count of days since 1970-01-01 into a DATE; it reverses UNIX_DATE.

name: GoogleSQL DATE_SUB()
description: Subtracts a number of DAY, WEEK, MONTH, QUARTER or YEAR units from a DATE and returns the earlier DATE; month arithmetic that lands past a short month's end gives its last day.

name: GoogleSQL DATE_TRUNC()
description: Truncates a DATE down to the first day of the period containing it, at a granularity such as WEEK, MONTH, QUARTER or YEAR; WEEK starts on Sunday and ISOWEEK on Monday.

name: GoogleSQL FORMAT_DATE()
description: Formats a DATE as a STRING using a format string made of elements such as %Y for the year, %m for the month and %d for the day.

name: GoogleSQL FORMAT_TIMESTAMP()
description: Formats a TIMESTAMP as a STRING using a format string of elements such as %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S, shown in an optional time zone.

name: GoogleSQL GENERATE_DATE_ARRAY()
description: Returns an array of DATE values from a start date to an end date, stepping one day by default or by an INTERVAL of days, weeks, months, quarters or years.

name: GoogleSQL JUSTIFY_INTERVAL()
description: Normalizes an INTERVAL by carrying every 24 hours of the time part into days and every 30 days into months, so 29 days and 49 hours becomes 1 month, 1 day and 1 hour.

name: GoogleSQL MAKE_INTERVAL()
description: Builds an INTERVAL from optional INT64 year, month, day, hour, minute and second arguments, each defaulting to 0 and passable by name, for example hour set to 10.

name: GoogleSQL PARSE_DATE()
description: Converts a STRING to a DATE using a format string; each element must match at the same position or an error is raised, and unspecified fields default from 1970-01-01.

name: GoogleSQL PARSE_TIMESTAMP()
description: Converts a STRING to a TIMESTAMP using a format string and an optional time zone; a mismatch raises an error, and unspecified fields default from 1970-01-01 00:00:00.

name: GoogleSQL TIMESTAMP()
description: Constructs a TIMESTAMP from a STRING holding a timestamp literal or from a DATE, read in an optional time zone; a DATE becomes the start of that day.

name: GoogleSQL TIMESTAMP_ADD()
description: Adds a whole number of units from NANOSECOND up to DAY to a TIMESTAMP and returns the later TIMESTAMP; a DAY is always 24 hours, independent of time zones.

name: GoogleSQL TIMESTAMP_DIFF()
description: Returns, as INT64, the number of units from NANOSECOND up to DAY between an end TIMESTAMP and a start TIMESTAMP, zero or negative when the end is earlier; fractions are truncated.

name: GoogleSQL TIMESTAMP_MICROS()
description: Converts an INT64 count of microseconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC into a TIMESTAMP.

name: GoogleSQL TIMESTAMP_MILLIS()
description: Converts an INT64 count of milliseconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC into a TIMESTAMP.

name: GoogleSQL TIMESTAMP_SECONDS()
description: Converts an INT64 count of seconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC into a TIMESTAMP.

name: GoogleSQL TIMESTAMP_SUB()
description: Subtracts a whole number of units from NANOSECOND up to DAY from a TIMESTAMP and returns the earlier TIMESTAMP; a DAY is always 24 hours, independent of time zones.

name: GoogleSQL TIMESTAMP_TRUNC()
description: Truncates a TIMESTAMP down to the start of a granularity such as SECOND, MINUTE, HOUR, DAY, MONTH or YEAR, evaluated in an optional time zone, and returns a TIMESTAMP.

name: GoogleSQL UNIX_DATE()
description: Returns the number of days from 1970-01-01 to a DATE as an INT64; it reverses DATE_FROM_UNIX_DATE.

name: GoogleSQL UNIX_MICROS()
description: Converts a TIMESTAMP into an INT64 count of microseconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC, keeping more precision than UNIX_MILLIS or UNIX_SECONDS.

name: GoogleSQL UNIX_MILLIS()
description: Converts a TIMESTAMP into an INT64 count of milliseconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC, dropping any finer precision.

name: GoogleSQL UNIX_SECONDS()
description: Converts a TIMESTAMP into an INT64 count of seconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC, dropping any finer precision.

name: GoogleSQL ADDDATE()
description: A synonym of DATE_ADD: adds an INTERVAL of a whole number of date-part units to a DATE and returns the new DATE.

name: GoogleSQL SUBDATE()
description: A synonym of DATE_SUB: subtracts an INTERVAL of a whole number of date-part units from a DATE and returns the new, earlier DATE.

name: PostgreSQL database dialect
description: Creates a Spanner database that uses the PostgreSQL dialect, so schemas, queries and clients follow PostgreSQL syntax, types and catalogs; the dialect is chosen when the database is created.

name: PostgreSQL generate_series()
description: Set-returning function that produces a series of integer or numeric values from a start to an end value with an optional step, one row per value, and is used in the FROM clause.
notes: Series in FROM; integer start/end/step cases.

name: PostgreSQL spanner.split_substr()
description: Splits a text value on a literal delimiter and returns a run of consecutive parts, from a chosen starting split for an optional count of splits; a negative start counts from the end.
notes: Documented positional substring splitting.

name: PostgreSQL make_interval()
description: Builds an interval value from optional years, months, weeks, days, hours, minutes and seconds fields, each of which defaults to zero when omitted.
notes: Documented interval construction.

name: PostgreSQL ILIKE operator
description: Case-insensitive pattern match that returns true when a string matches a pattern with percent and underscore wildcards, ignoring letter case; an optional ESCAPE clause names the escape character.
notes: Case-insensitive matching and escape handling.

name: PostgreSQL !~~ operator
description: Operator spelling of NOT LIKE: returns true when the string does not match the pattern, using case-sensitive wildcard matching, unlike the case-insensitive !~~* form.
notes: Negated LIKE mapping.

name: PostgreSQL regexp_replace() first-match semantics
description: Replaces the part of a string matched by the first occurrence of a POSIX regular expression with the replacement text, leaving any later matches in the string unchanged.
notes: Corrects replacement behavior.

name: PostgreSQL SUM(float8) on empty input
description: Adding up a float8 column over zero rows returns NULL rather than zero, so an empty result set gives a NULL double precision sum.

name: PostgreSQL SUM(float8) on all-NULL input
description: SUM ignores NULL inputs, so when every float8 value is NULL there is nothing to add and the sum is NULL instead of zero.

name: PostgreSQL AVG(float8) on empty input
description: The average of a float8 column over zero rows is NULL, because there are no values to divide a total by.

name: PostgreSQL AVG(float8) on all-NULL input
description: AVG skips NULL inputs, so when every float8 value is NULL there is nothing to average and the result is NULL.

name: PostgreSQL ARRAY_AGG(UUID)
description: Collects UUID values from the input rows into a single array of UUIDs, keeping NULLs, with an optional ORDER BY inside the call to sort the elements.
notes: Preserves native UUID results.

name: PostgreSQL pg_am
description: Catalog table listing the access methods available for tables and indexes, giving each method's name and type.
notes: Populated or static local catalog; not a complete PostgreSQL server catalog.

name: PostgreSQL pg_attrdef
description: Catalog table holding column default expressions, linking each table and column number to the text of its default value.
notes: Populated or static local catalog; not a complete PostgreSQL server catalog.

name: PostgreSQL pg_attribute
description: Catalog table with one row per table column, giving its name, data type, position and whether it is NOT NULL or has a default, identity or generated value.
notes: Populated or static local catalog; not a complete PostgreSQL server catalog.

name: PostgreSQL pg_class
description: Catalog table of relations such as tables, indexes, views and sequences, giving each one's name, schema, kind and column count.
notes: Populated or static local catalog; not a complete PostgreSQL server catalog.

name: PostgreSQL pg_collation
description: Catalog table listing the collations that can be used to order and compare text, with each collation's name, schema and encoding.
notes: Populated or static local catalog; not a complete PostgreSQL server catalog.

name: PostgreSQL pg_constraint
description: Catalog table of table constraints such as primary keys, foreign keys and check constraints, showing the constrained columns and the referenced table.
notes: Populated or static local catalog; not a complete PostgreSQL server catalog.

name: PostgreSQL pg_index
description: Catalog table with one row per index, naming the indexed table and the number of key columns and flagging whether it is unique, primary or valid.
notes: Populated or static local catalog; not a complete PostgreSQL server catalog.

name: PostgreSQL pg_indexes
description: Catalog view listing each index with its schema, table name, index name and the text of the statement that defines it.
notes: Populated or static local catalog; not a complete PostgreSQL server catalog.

name: PostgreSQL pg_namespace
description: Catalog table of schemas, giving each schema's name and identifier, including the public schema and the system schemas.
notes: Populated or static local catalog; not a complete PostgreSQL server catalog.

name: PostgreSQL pg_sequence
description: Catalog table with the settings of each sequence, such as its data type, start value, cache size and whether it cycles.
notes: Populated or static local catalog; not a complete PostgreSQL server catalog.

name: PostgreSQL pg_sequences
description: Catalog view that presents sequences by schema and name together with their configured properties, such as start value and cycling.
notes: Populated or static local catalog; not a complete PostgreSQL server catalog.

name: PostgreSQL pg_settings
description: Catalog view of configuration parameters, giving each setting's name, current value and description.
notes: Populated or static local catalog; not a complete PostgreSQL server catalog.

name: PostgreSQL pg_tables
description: Catalog view listing the tables of the database by schema name and table name.
notes: Populated or static local catalog; not a complete PostgreSQL server catalog.

name: PostgreSQL pg_type
description: Catalog table of data types, giving each type's name, schema, length, category and the element or array type it relates to.
notes: Populated or static local catalog; not a complete PostgreSQL server catalog.

name: PostgreSQL pg_views
description: Catalog view listing views by schema and view name together with the query text that defines each view.
notes: Populated or static local catalog; not a complete PostgreSQL server catalog.

name: PostgreSQL pg_proc named-schema UDF metadata
description: Catalog table of functions with their name, schema, kind, argument types, return type and SQL body; user-defined functions in a named schema report that schema.
notes: Correct function/schema metadata.

name: PostgreSQL catalog role filtering
description: Under fine-grained access control, queries on the catalog tables return only rows for schema objects that the querying database role has been granted privileges on.
notes: Filters object rows by creator_role privileges.

name: PostgreSQL CREATE TABLE SYNONYM
description: A SYNONYM clause on CREATE TABLE gives the new table one extra name that queries and DML can use as an alias; the alias cannot be used in DDL or schema changes.

name: PostgreSQL ALTER TABLE ADD SYNONYM
description: Adds an alternate name to an existing table so applications can read and write it under either name; a table can hold one synonym, and DDL must still use the real name.

name: PostgreSQL ALTER TABLE DROP SYNONYM
description: Removes the alternate name from a table once applications no longer use it, leaving the table and its original name unchanged.

name: PostgreSQL CREATE VIEW
description: Defines a named view over a SELECT query; the PostgreSQL dialect takes a SQL SECURITY clause that says whether the view runs with the caller's or the definer's privileges.

name: PostgreSQL CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW
description: Creates a view or, if it already exists, replaces its query or security type in place instead of failing the way plain CREATE VIEW does.

name: PostgreSQL DROP VIEW
description: Removes a view definition; only the view is dropped, and the tables or views it queries are left untouched.

name: PostgreSQL CREATE CHANGE STREAM
description: Defines a change stream that records inserts, updates and deletes for the whole database or chosen tables and columns, with WITH options such as retention period and value capture type.
notes: Partition distribution is simulated; restart behavior is tracked separately.

name: PostgreSQL ALTER CHANGE STREAM
description: Changes an existing change stream: the tables and columns it watches, or its WITH options such as retention period, value capture type and the exclude filters.
notes: Partition distribution is simulated; restart behavior is tracked separately.

name: PostgreSQL DROP CHANGE STREAM
description: Removes a change stream so it stops recording data changes and its read function is no longer available.
notes: Partition distribution is simulated; restart behavior is tracked separately.

name: PostgreSQL spanner.read_json_<stream>()
description: Read function created with each PostgreSQL-dialect change stream, named by appending the stream name; takes start and end timestamps, partition token, heartbeat interval and read options, and returns JSON change records.
notes: Partition distribution is simulated; restart behavior is tracked separately.

name: PostgreSQL JSONB type
description: PostgreSQL-dialect type for JSON documents kept in a normalized form: whitespace and key order are not preserved, duplicate keys keep the last value, and JSON null differs from SQL NULL.
notes: Spanner JSONB semantics, not PostgreSQL semantics.

name: PostgreSQL JSONB concatenation order
description: The JSONB concatenation operator joins two values: two arrays give one array with all left elements followed by all right elements, and two objects give the merged keys with the right value winning.
notes: Preserves left operand elements before right operand.

name: PostgreSQL JSONB negative-index ->
description: The JSONB single-arrow operator with an integer returns that zero-based array element as JSONB; a negative index does not count from the end and returns SQL NULL.
notes: Returns NULL per Spanner behavior.

name: PostgreSQL JSONB negative-index ->>
description: The JSONB double-arrow operator with an integer returns that array element as text rather than JSONB; a negative index does not count from the end and returns SQL NULL.
notes: Returns NULL per Spanner behavior.

name: PostgreSQL JSONB large numbers on macOS
description: JSONB keeps number values as written, including trailing zeros, with up to 4,932 digits before the decimal point and 16,383 after it, so very large integers and precise decimals are not rounded.
notes: Up to 4,932 integer digits.

name: PostgreSQL TABLESAMPLE BERNOULLI
description: Row-sampling clause that independently keeps each row with a probability given as a percentage from 0 to 100, so the sample is roughly that share of the table and its size varies.
notes: PostgreSQL REPEATABLE remains rejected.

name: PostgreSQL TABLESAMPLE SPANNER.RESERVOIR
description: Row-sampling clause that takes a fixed row count and returns exactly that many randomly chosen rows, or the whole input when it has fewer rows than requested.
notes: PostgreSQL REPEATABLE remains rejected.

name: SpannerService.ExecuteBatchDml
description: Runs several DML statements one after another in a single request, within the request's read-write transaction, and returns one result per statement; execution stops after the first failed statement.

name: Batch DML sequence-number handling
description: Each batch DML request carries an increasing per-transaction sequence number that makes it idempotent, so a replayed request returns the original response instead of running twice.

name: SpannerService.BatchWrite
description: Applies groups of mutations in efficient transactions, each group committed atomically, and streams back one result per group; the groups must be independent of each other.

name: Insert mutation
description: Adds new rows to a table; if a row with the same primary key already exists, the whole write fails with ALREADY_EXISTS.

name: InsertOrUpdate mutation
description: Writes rows by inserting those with new keys and, for keys that already exist, overwriting only the supplied columns while leaving the other columns as they were.

name: Replace mutation
description: Writes rows by deleting any existing row with the same key and inserting the supplied values, so columns that are not supplied become NULL.

name: Update mutation
description: Changes columns of rows that already exist and leaves the unspecified columns alone; if a named row does not exist the write fails with NOT_FOUND.

name: Delete mutation by key
description: Removes rows identified by an explicit list of primary keys; the mutation succeeds whether or not the named rows exist.

name: Delete mutation by key range
description: Removes every row whose primary key falls inside a start and end key range, each end open or closed, in a single mutation; a range that matches no rows is not an error.

name: INSERT statement
description: Adds rows to a table from a VALUES list or the result of a query; if a primary key is already present the statement fails with a duplicate-key error.

name: UPDATE statement
description: Changes column values of the rows chosen by a required WHERE clause using SET assignments, and reports how many rows were modified.

name: DELETE statement
description: Removes the rows chosen by a required WHERE clause from a table, also deleting interleaved child rows that cascade, and reports how many rows were deleted.

name: Partitioned DML execution
description: Runs one UPDATE or DELETE across a whole table by splitting the key space and executing it in separate smaller transactions; the statement must be idempotent and fully partitionable.
notes: Local execution; no distributed parallelism.

name: GoogleSQL INSERT OR IGNORE
description: Inserts the rows whose primary key is new and silently skips rows whose key already exists, instead of failing the statement with a duplicate-key error.

name: GoogleSQL INSERT OR UPDATE
description: Inserts a row when its primary key is new, otherwise updates the existing row with the supplied values and leaves columns not named in the statement unchanged.

name: PostgreSQL ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
description: PostgreSQL-style clause on INSERT that skips a row whose key conflicts with an existing primary key or unique index entry instead of raising a duplicate-key error.

name: PostgreSQL ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE
description: PostgreSQL-style clause on INSERT that, when the named conflict target already exists, applies a SET list to the existing row and can read the proposed values through the EXCLUDED alias.

name: GoogleSQL THEN RETURN
description: Clause on INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE that returns chosen columns or expressions of the affected rows, such as default or generated values, from the same statement without a separate SELECT.

name: GoogleSQL THEN RETURN WITH ACTION
description: Extends THEN RETURN with an extra last string column, named ACTION unless aliased, that tells for each returned row whether it was inserted, updated or deleted.

name: PostgreSQL RETURNING
description: PostgreSQL-dialect spelling of returning data from a write: a RETURNING list on INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE yields the affected rows' columns or expressions, such as defaults or generated values.

name: SpannerService.BeginTransaction
description: Starts a transaction on a session, read-write, read-only or partitioned DML, and returns its ID for later requests; often skipped because other calls can begin one implicitly.

name: SpannerService.Commit
description: Commits a transaction by atomically applying the supplied mutations to the database and returns the commit timestamp; an ABORTED error means the transaction must be retried.

name: SpannerService.Rollback
description: Aborts a transaction and releases any locks it holds; used when a transaction that has already read or queried data decides not to commit.

name: CommitStats mutation_count
description: Commit statistics returned on request that report how many mutations the transaction applied, so clients can track how large their commits are.
notes: Local documented mutation counting; index/constraint differences remain possible.

name: max_commit_delay delay effect
description: An optional commit setting that lets Spanner hold a commit for a short, bounded time so it can be grouped with others, trading a little latency for higher throughput.
notes: LocalCloud validates 0–500 ms but does not delay commits.

name: Read-write transaction read/query/write buffering
description: A read-write transaction runs reads, queries and DML against a consistent view of the data, while mutations are held back and applied atomically together when the transaction commits.

name: Read-only transactions
description: Run several reads and queries at one consistent snapshot timestamp without taking locks or blocking writers; they cannot modify data and use a chosen timestamp bound.

name: PENDING_COMMIT_TIMESTAMP()
description: Returns a placeholder that Spanner replaces with the transaction's actual commit timestamp when it commits, for writing into a TIMESTAMP column from INSERT or UPDATE statements.

name: allow_commit_timestamp columns
description: Column option that lets a TIMESTAMP column be filled with the transaction's commit timestamp at write time, which gives each row a reliable record of when it was last written.

name: Strong reads
description: The default read mode: it sees every transaction committed before the read began, and all rows returned are consistent with each other, but two strong reads in a row can see different data.

name: Exact read timestamp
description: Reads the database as it was at one explicit timestamp chosen by the caller, which makes the result repeatable; the timestamp cannot be older than the database's earliest version time.

name: Exact staleness reads
description: Reads data as of a fixed length of time before the read starts, such as a chosen number of seconds earlier, which lets a nearby replica serve the read without waiting.

name: Bounded staleness reads
description: Lets Spanner pick the newest read timestamp within a maximum staleness or after a minimum timestamp that a nearby replica can serve without blocking; allowed only for single-use read-only reads.

name: Read-your-writes in a read-write transaction
description: Within a read-write transaction, queries and reads see the changes made earlier in that same transaction by DML statements, before the transaction commits.

name: SELECT FOR UPDATE exclusive locking
description: A FOR UPDATE clause on a SELECT takes exclusive locks on the cells it scans until the read-write transaction ends, so other writers wait and contention causes fewer aborts.
notes: Acquires exclusive locks.

name: ABORTED transaction retries
description: When Spanner aborts a read-write transaction, for example because of lock conflicts, the call fails with ABORTED and the application should run the whole transaction again from the start.
notes: Local error-state matrix has documented limitations.

name: Failed-transaction state validation
description: A transaction that has been aborted, committed or rolled back is finished; further reads or writes on it return an error and the work must be run again in a new transaction.
notes: Local error-state matrix has documented limitations.

name: SERIALIZABLE isolation
description: The default isolation level: transactions behave as if run one at a time in commit order, giving external consistency, and conflicting transactions may be aborted and need a retry.

name: REPEATABLE_READ snapshot isolation
description: Isolation level implemented as snapshot isolation: all reads in a transaction see the snapshot from its start, concurrent writes to the same data succeed only if they do not conflict, and write skew is possible.
notes: Snapshot at first read; validates write conflicts at commit.

name: Disjoint read-write transactions commit concurrently
description: Read-write transactions that touch different rows or key ranges take separate locks and do not block one another, so they can proceed and commit at the same time.
notes: Key/range locks instead of whole-database exclusive concurrency.

name: Wound-wait lock waiting
description: Deadlock-avoidance scheme for lock conflicts: an older transaction can abort, or wound, a younger one holding a lock it needs, while a younger one waits for an older one, so the oldest always progresses.
notes: Configurable timeout; RPC-deadline handling differs from production.

name: Deadlock aborts one transaction
description: When two transactions each hold a lock the other needs, Spanner aborts one of them with ABORTED so the other can finish, and the aborted transaction must be retried.
notes: Two-key deadlock regression; retries still needed.

name: CREATE INDEX
description: Creates a secondary index on one or more columns of a table, ordered by the index keys, so queries that filter or sort on them can avoid scanning the whole table.

name: DROP INDEX
description: Removes a secondary index; queries that used it fall back to other access paths, and the base table data is unaffected.

name: NULL_FILTERED indexes
description: GoogleSQL index option that leaves out rows where any index key column is NULL, giving a smaller index; the PostgreSQL dialect expresses it with a WHERE column IS NOT NULL clause.

name: GoogleSQL STORING index columns
description: The STORING clause copies extra non-key columns into the index, so queries that filter on the index keys and select those columns can be answered from the index without reading the base table.

name: PostgreSQL INCLUDE index columns
description: The PostgreSQL-dialect INCLUDE clause stores extra non-key columns in the index entries, the counterpart of GoogleSQL STORING, so index-only reads can return them.

name: Index backfill
description: When an index is created on a table that already has rows, Spanner populates it with entries for the existing data in the background as part of a long-running schema change.
notes: Synchronous local backfill; no production scheduling model.

name: Unique-index validation
description: A UNIQUE index requires each combination of indexed key values to appear in only one row; a write that would duplicate one fails, as does creating the index over data that already has duplicates.

name: Unique-index conflict recheck at commit
description: Uniqueness is enforced when a transaction commits, so two concurrent transactions that write the same unique index key cannot both succeed.
notes: Prevents duplicates across concurrent buffered writes.

name: Foreign-key validation
description: A foreign key requires each value in the referencing columns to match an existing row of the referenced table, and writes that would leave a dangling reference are rejected.

name: Foreign-key ON DELETE CASCADE
description: Foreign-key action that automatically deletes the referencing rows when the row they reference is deleted.

name: Foreign-key ON DELETE NO ACTION
description: The default foreign-key action: deleting a referenced row is rejected while rows still reference it, so the write fails instead of changing the referencing rows.

name: CHECK constraint validation
description: A CHECK constraint states a boolean expression over a row's columns; inserts or updates that would make it false are rejected, and existing rows are validated when the constraint is added.

name: Generated-column evaluation
description: The value of a generated column is computed from an expression over other columns of the same row, cannot be written directly, and is recalculated when the columns it uses change.

name: IDENTITY columns
description: Column attribute GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY that fills the column with automatically generated, bit-reversed positive integers when no value is given; an explicit value can still be written.
notes: Persistence of allocated counters is tracked under sequences.

name: Column DEFAULT expressions
description: Gives a column an expression that supplies its value when an INSERT omits the column; the expression cannot reference other columns and may be nondeterministic.

name: ON UPDATE column expressions
description: Sets a column to its expression value, typically the commit timestamp, automatically whenever a non-key column of the row is updated, giving a last-modified time without extra code.

name: GoogleSQL CREATE CHANGE STREAM
description: Defines a change stream that records inserts, updates and deletes for the whole database or listed tables and columns, with OPTIONS such as retention_period and value_capture_type.

name: GoogleSQL ALTER CHANGE STREAM
description: Changes an existing change stream: what it watches, or its OPTIONS such as retention_period, value_capture_type and the exclude filters.

name: GoogleSQL DROP CHANGE STREAM
description: Deletes a change stream so it stops recording data changes and its READ function disappears; the tables it watched are not affected.

name: Change stream FOR ALL
description: Change stream scope that watches every table and column in the database, including tables and columns added later, instead of a named list.

name: Change stream table/column lists
description: Change stream scope naming specific tables, optionally with chosen columns: a table alone watches all its columns, while listing columns watches only those plus the primary key.

name: Change stream OLD_AND_NEW_VALUES
description: The default value capture type: each data change record holds the old and new values of the columns that were modified, plus the primary key, but not unchanged columns.

name: Change stream NEW_VALUES
description: Value capture type that records only the new values of the modified non-key columns and no old values.

name: Change stream NEW_ROW
description: Value capture type that records the full new row, every watched column whether modified or not, whenever any of them changes, with no old values.

name: Change stream NEW_ROW_AND_OLD_VALUES
description: Value capture type that records the full new row, modified and unmodified columns, together with the old values of the modified columns.

name: GoogleSQL READ_<stream>()
description: Function Spanner creates for each change stream, named READ_ followed by the stream name; it takes start_timestamp, end_timestamp, partition_token, heartbeat_milliseconds and read_options, and returns ChangeRecord rows.

name: Change-stream heartbeat records
description: Records returned when a partition has no data changes, carrying a timestamp that promises all changes at or before it were delivered; their rate is set by heartbeat_milliseconds.

name: Change-stream child-partition records
description: Records announcing partitions created when one splits or merges, listing each child's partition token, its parent tokens and the start timestamp from which to query it.

name: Change-stream resume-token continuation
description: A reader that stops can continue by querying again from the last timestamp it processed with the partition token it was reading, instead of rereading the stream from the start.
notes: Token records timestamp, partition and record index.

name: Change-stream scan-boundary commit capture
description: Every committed change matching the stream is returned exactly once in commit-timestamp order, including a change committed exactly at the start or end timestamp of a query range.
notes: Regression covers commit exactly on a scan-window boundary.

name: Change-stream Update mutation records
description: A change made by an Update mutation is recorded as a data change record with mod type UPDATE, whose keys, column types and new values describe the primary key and the modified columns.
notes: Captures update columns with the correct column/value alignment.

name: Change-stream user transaction tags
description: Each data change record carries the transaction tag of the transaction that made the change, so consumers can tell writes apart by application or purpose, plus a flag for system transactions.
notes: Propagates supplied transaction tags.

name: Change-stream child query starting before child start
description: A child partition must be queried with a start timestamp at or after the start_timestamp of the child partition record that announced it; earlier changes come from the parent partition.
notes: Clamps to child start; avoids a stalled child query.

name: exclude_insert stream option
description: Change stream option that, when true, leaves INSERT modifications out of the stream so new rows are not reported, while updates and deletes are still recorded; the default is false.

name: exclude_update stream option
description: Change stream option that, when true, leaves UPDATE modifications out of the stream so changes to existing rows are not reported, while inserts and deletes are still recorded; the default is false.

name: exclude_delete stream option
description: Change stream option that, when true, leaves DELETE modifications out of the stream so removed rows are not reported, while inserts and updates are still recorded; the default is false.

name: allow_txn_exclusion stream option
description: Change stream option, false by default, that when true lets the stream honor write transactions marked with exclude_txn_from_change_streams so their changes are not recorded.

name: exclude_txn_from_change_streams request option
description: Boolean option on a write transaction or batch write asking change streams not to record its changes; it only applies to streams with allow_txn_exclusion enabled and is invalid for read-only transactions.

name: MUTABLE_KEY_RANGE partition-start deduplication
description: A change stream partition owns an immutable key range for a time range, and readers learn of each new partition once, through a child partition record naming its token and start timestamp.
notes: Emits move-in start record once, not on every scan.

name: Change-stream partition split
description: When load or size grows, Spanner can split a partition's key range; the old partition ends with child partition records naming the new partitions, each listing the old token as its parent.
notes: Emits partition lifecycle records locally; churn is timer-driven, not production load-driven partition management.

name: Change-stream partition merge
description: Spanner can merge partitions covering adjacent key ranges into one new partition; its child partition record lists several parent tokens, and its changes should be processed after all parents are done.
notes: Emits partition lifecycle records locally; churn is timer-driven, not production load-driven partition management.

name: Change-stream partition move
description: When Spanner changes how a key range is served, the partition for that range is replaced by a new one announced through a child partition record, and readers continue with the new token.
notes: Emits partition lifecycle records locally; churn is timer-driven, not production load-driven partition management.

name: Change-stream retention cleanup
description: Change records older than the stream's retention_period, between one and thirty days with seven as the default, are removed, so queries cannot start before the retained window.
notes: Runs on churn cycles; disabled when churning is disabled.

name: CREATE SEARCH INDEX
description: Creates a search index over one or more TOKENLIST columns, with optional stored columns, partitioning, ordering and options such as sort_order_sharding, to speed up full-text, substring and exact-match queries.

name: DROP SEARCH INDEX
description: Removes a search index; IF EXISTS makes the statement succeed when the index is absent, and the base table with its TOKENLIST columns stays in place.

name: ALTER SEARCH INDEX ADD stored column
description: Adds a column to the stored columns of a search index so queries can read it straight from the index; GoogleSQL writes ADD STORED COLUMN and PostgreSQL writes ADD INCLUDE COLUMN.
notes: Both dialects; validates columns and dependencies.

name: ALTER SEARCH INDEX DROP stored column
description: Removes a column from the stored columns of a search index, so the index no longer holds a copy of it; GoogleSQL writes DROP STORED COLUMN and PostgreSQL writes DROP INCLUDE COLUMN.
notes: Both dialects; validates columns and dependencies.

name: PostgreSQL search-index DDL round trip
description: In a PostgreSQL-dialect database, the DDL returned for the database includes CREATE SEARCH INDEX statements in PostgreSQL syntax that can be replayed to rebuild the same indexes.
notes: GetDatabaseDdl emits replayable CREATE SEARCH INDEX.

name: SEARCH()
description: Returns TRUE when a full-text query matches a TOKENLIST built by TOKENIZE_FULLTEXT; queries use rquery syntax by default, or the words and words_phrase dialects, and it is used in WHERE.

name: SEARCH_SUBSTRING()
description: Returns TRUE when a substring query occurs in a TOKENLIST built by TOKENIZE_SUBSTRING, ignoring case; relative_search_type can require phrase, prefix or suffix placement.

name: SEARCH_NGRAMS()
description: Fuzzy-match predicate that returns TRUE when enough distinct n-grams of the query appear in an n-gram TOKENLIST, set by min_ngrams or min_ngrams_percent, which tolerates misspellings.

name: SNIPPET() documented JSON shape
description: Returns JSON holding a list of snippets, each with the snippet text, the begin and end positions of matched terms to highlight, and the source range of the original text.
notes: begin/end highlight strings plus source bounds.

name: Search over SQL NULL token lists
description: SEARCH and the related search functions return NULL when the TOKENLIST or the query is NULL, so such rows never match a search predicate in WHERE.
notes: No crash or spurious match.

name: Unicode RQUERY terms
description: Search queries in the default rquery syntax may contain terms in any language or Unicode script, and are tokenized the same way as the indexed text.
notes: Parses UTF-8 terms.

name: TOKENIZE_FULLTEXT()
description: Builds a full-text TOKENLIST from a string or string array by splitting it into lowercase word tokens, with options such as language_tag, content_type, token_category and remove_diacritics.
notes: Supported local tokenization; parameter-specific effects have separate rows.

name: TOKENIZE_SUBSTRING()
description: Builds a substring TOKENLIST by lowercasing each word and generating n-grams between ngram_size_min and ngram_size_max, so SEARCH_SUBSTRING can find partial words; also offers relative_search_types.
notes: Supported local tokenization; parameter-specific effects have separate rows.

name: TOKENIZE_NGRAMS()
description: Builds an n-gram TOKENLIST from the whole input without splitting it into words, producing all n-grams of the configured sizes for fuzzy SEARCH_NGRAMS matching and regular-expression acceleration.
notes: Supported local tokenization; parameter-specific effects have separate rows.

name: TOKENIZE_NUMBER()
description: Builds a numeric TOKENLIST from integer or floating-point values, using an algorithm such as logtree, prefixtree or floatingpoint, to speed up equality and range comparisons.
notes: Supported local tokenization; parameter-specific effects have separate rows.

name: TOKENIZE_BOOL()
description: Builds a TOKENLIST from a BOOL or array of BOOL, producing the token y for TRUE and n for FALSE, to speed up boolean equality predicates.
notes: Supported local tokenization; parameter-specific effects have separate rows.

name: TOKENIZE_EXACT_MATCH()
description: Exact-match tokenization that turns a whole value into a single verbatim token, so equality lookups can use a search index; no case folding or word splitting is applied.
notes: Supported local tokenization; parameter-specific effects have separate rows.

name: TOKEN()
description: Constructs an exact-match TOKENLIST from a bytes or string value, or an array of them, tokenized verbatim to accelerate equality and ARRAY_INCLUDES predicates; NULL input gives NULL.
notes: Supported local tokenization; parameter-specific effects have separate rows.

name: TOKENLIST_CONCAT()
description: Combines several TOKENLIST values, all produced by TOKENIZE_FULLTEXT or all by TOKENIZE_SUBSTRING, into one so a single search covers several columns; a NULL element counts as an empty list.
notes: Supported local tokenization; parameter-specific effects have separate rows.

name: HTML full-text tokenization
description: Setting content_type to text/html in TOKENIZE_FULLTEXT removes HTML tags, decodes escaped entities, and assigns each token a category by prominence, such as title or large text.
notes: HTML 4 entities; excludes script/style content.

name: French language_tag tokenization
description: Passing the language tag fr to TOKENIZE_FULLTEXT applies French word-splitting rules instead of automatic language detection, which changes how some French phrases are split into tokens.
notes: Documented French behavior; not every language independently verified.

name: short_tokens_only_for_anchors effect
description: TOKENIZE_SUBSTRING option that, when TRUE, omits short n-grams below ngram_size_max except those needed for prefix and suffix relative searches, shrinking the index; the default is FALSE.
notes: Applies short-token anchoring behavior.

name: Mixed remove_diacritics TOKENLIST_CONCAT
description: TOKENLIST_CONCAT merges token lists from one tokenizer function into a single list; each source list can use remove_diacritics, which strips accents from text and queries so accented and plain forms match.
notes: Handles mixed token-list settings.

name: PostgreSQL spanner.tokenize_substring relative_search_types
description: Option of the PostgreSQL spanner.tokenize_substring function: an array of relative search types such as phrase, value_prefix, value_suffix, word_prefix, word_suffix or all, for which extra anchor tokens are generated.
notes: Avoids the prior crash and applies supported relative options.

name: DEBUG_TOKENLIST() output format
description: Returns a human-readable string of the tokens in a TOKENLIST, showing token text, attributes and positions; meant for debugging, and its format may change without notice.
notes: Matches documented examples.

name: SCORE() local score
description: Calculates a relevance score for a full-text TOKENLIST against a search query, higher meaning a stronger match; it returns FLOAT64, needs SEARCH in the same query, and is typically used in ORDER BY.
notes: Deterministic local relevance, not production relevance.

name: SCORE_NGRAMS() local score
description: Calculates a fuzzy-match relevance score for an n-gram TOKENLIST against a query using trigram overlap, higher meaning more similar; it returns 0 when the TOKENLIST or query is NULL.
notes: Deterministic local n-gram score.

name: SCORE token_category_weights
description: Option in the SCORE options JSON that sets a multiplier for each HTML token category (small, medium, large and title), so matches in prominent text such as titles can count for more.
notes: Applies provided category weights.

name: SCORE version option effect
description: Option in the SCORE options JSON that selects a specific release of the scoring algorithm so scores stay stable as the scorer improves; the score_version database option sets a database-wide default.
notes: Accepts version without changing local scoring.

name: SCORE_NGRAMS array_aggregator
description: SCORE_NGRAMS argument for TOKENLISTs over ARRAY columns: flatten, the default, scores the array as one joined string, while max_element scores each element separately and returns the highest.
notes: GoogleSQL aggregation option.

name: GoogleSQL COSINE_DISTANCE()
description: Returns the cosine distance between two equal-length vectors given as arrays of FLOAT32 or FLOAT64, one minus their cosine similarity, so smaller means more alike; zero vectors raise an error.

name: GoogleSQL DOT_PRODUCT()
description: Returns the dot product of two equal-length vectors given as arrays of INT64, FLOAT32 or FLOAT64, the sum of the products of corresponding elements, as FLOAT64.

name: GoogleSQL EUCLIDEAN_DISTANCE()
description: Returns the straight-line (L2) distance between two equal-length vectors given as arrays of FLOAT32 or FLOAT64, as FLOAT64; zero means the vectors are identical.

name: PostgreSQL spanner.cosine_distance()
description: PostgreSQL-dialect function that returns the cosine distance between two float4 or float8 arrays of the same length, used to rank rows by similarity in exact nearest-neighbor queries.
notes: float4[]/float8[] signatures; DOT_PRODUCT also int8[].

name: PostgreSQL spanner.euclidean_distance()
description: PostgreSQL-dialect function that returns the straight-line (Euclidean) distance between two float4 or float8 arrays of the same length, used to find the closest vectors.
notes: float4[]/float8[] signatures; DOT_PRODUCT also int8[].

name: PostgreSQL spanner.dot_product()
description: PostgreSQL-dialect function that returns the dot product of two equal-length numeric arrays, the sum of the products of corresponding elements, usable to rank vectors by similarity.
notes: float4[]/float8[] signatures; DOT_PRODUCT also int8[].

name: GoogleSQL APPROX_COSINE_DISTANCE()
description: Approximates the cosine distance between an embedding column and a constant query vector using a vector index; it must be the only ORDER BY key, followed by LIMIT, and an options argument tunes the search.
notes: Returns exact nearest neighbors; no ANN recall/latency simulation.

name: GoogleSQL APPROX_DOT_PRODUCT()
description: Approximates the dot product between an embedding column and a constant query vector using a vector index, for ORDER BY with LIMIT queries that find approximate nearest neighbors.
notes: Returns exact nearest neighbors; no ANN recall/latency simulation.

name: GoogleSQL APPROX_EUCLIDEAN_DISTANCE()
description: Approximates the Euclidean distance between an embedding column and a constant query vector using a vector index, trading some recall for lower latency than the exact EUCLIDEAN_DISTANCE.
notes: Returns exact nearest neighbors; no ANN recall/latency simulation.

name: GoogleSQL CREATE VECTOR INDEX
description: DDL statement that builds an approximate-nearest-neighbor index on an array embedding column; the distance_type option (COSINE, DOT_PRODUCT or EUCLIDEAN) is required and STORING adds columns for filtering.
notes: Validates index options; nearest-neighbor execution remains exact.

name: GoogleSQL ALTER VECTOR INDEX
description: DDL statement that changes an existing vector index by adding or dropping a stored column, setting options such as disable_search, or rebuilding the index in place to refresh its tree.
notes: Local validated metadata.

name: GoogleSQL DROP VECTOR INDEX
description: DDL statement that deletes a vector index by name, leaving the table and its embedding column and rows unchanged.
notes: Local validated metadata.

name: PostgreSQL CREATE INDEX USING ScaNN
description: PostgreSQL-dialect vector index: CREATE INDEX with USING scann on a float4 array column, INCLUDE for stored columns and WITH (distance_type = ...) to choose the distance metric.
notes: DDL accepted and printed back in replayable form.

name: PostgreSQL spanner.approx_cosine_distance()
description: PostgreSQL-dialect function that approximates the cosine distance between an embedding column and a constant vector through a ScaNN vector index, with a jsonb options argument to tune the search.
notes: Exact nearest neighbors; not a ScaNN ANN engine.

name: PostgreSQL spanner.approx_euclidean_distance()
description: PostgreSQL-dialect function that approximates the Euclidean distance between an embedding column and a constant vector through a vector index, used as the sole ORDER BY key with LIMIT.
notes: Exact nearest neighbors; not a ScaNN ANN engine.

name: PostgreSQL spanner.approx_dot_product()
description: PostgreSQL-dialect function that approximates the dot product between an embedding column and a constant vector through a vector index, for approximate nearest-neighbor queries with LIMIT.
notes: Exact nearest neighbors; not a ScaNN ANN engine.

name: ARRAY<FLOAT32> vector_length annotation
description: The vector_length annotation fixes the number of dimensions of a FLOAT32 array column used for embeddings; PostgreSQL writes it as a float4 array with VECTOR LENGTH after the type.
notes: Local validation; no dedicated vector storage engine.

name: ARRAY<FLOAT64> vector_length annotation
description: The vector_length annotation fixes the number of dimensions of a FLOAT64 array column used for double-precision embeddings, at twice the storage per element of FLOAT32; PostgreSQL uses VECTOR LENGTH.
notes: Local validation; no dedicated vector storage engine.

name: ANN recall/latency tuning
description: Approximate nearest neighbor queries trade recall for speed: scanning more leaves of the vector index, through num_leaves_to_search or pct_leaves_to_search, improves recall but raises latency and cost.
notes: Exact scans cannot model production ANN tuning.

name: num_leaves_to_search query tuning
description: Search option in the approximate distance functions' options JSON that sets how many vector index leaves to scan; it must be a positive integer and cannot be combined with pct_leaves_to_search.
notes: Validated but does not alter the exact scan.

name: GRAPH MATCH queries
description: GQL query that starts with GRAPH and a property graph name, uses MATCH to find nodes and edges fitting a pattern, and ends with RETURN, which produces the result rows.
notes: Shared reference evaluation; production limitations remain.

name: GQL path queries
description: GQL MATCH patterns that bind a whole path to a variable, often with variable-length hops, so path functions such as PATH_LENGTH, NODES and EDGES can inspect the matched paths.
notes: Shared reference evaluation; production limitations remain.

name: GoogleSQL DESTINATION_NODE_ID()
description: Takes a graph edge and returns, as a STRING, the unique identifier of the node the edge points to; the identifier is only meaningful within the query that produced it.

name: GoogleSQL EDGES()
description: Takes a graph path and returns its edges as an array of graph elements, in the order they appear along the path.

name: GoogleSQL ELEMENT_DEFINITION_NAME()
description: Returns, as a STRING, the name of the node table or edge table in the property graph definition that a given node or edge comes from.

name: GoogleSQL ELEMENT_ID()
description: Returns a STRING that uniquely identifies a graph node or edge; the identifier is valid only within the query that produced it.

name: GoogleSQL IS_ACYCLIC()
description: Takes a graph path and returns TRUE if no node appears in it more than once, and FALSE if any node repeats.

name: GoogleSQL IS_SIMPLE()
description: Takes a graph path and returns TRUE if no node repeats, except that the first and last node may be the same, so a closed loop still counts as simple.

name: GoogleSQL IS_TRAIL()
description: Takes a graph path and returns TRUE if no edge appears in it more than once, even if nodes repeat, and FALSE if any edge is traversed twice.

name: GoogleSQL LABELS()
description: Returns the labels of a graph node or edge as an array of STRING, keeping the original capitalization of each label.

name: GoogleSQL NODES()
description: Takes a graph path and returns its nodes as an array of graph elements, in the order they appear along the path.

name: GoogleSQL PATH_FIRST()
description: Takes a graph path and returns its first node, the node where the path starts.

name: GoogleSQL PATH_LAST()
description: Takes a graph path and returns its last node, the node where the path ends.

name: GoogleSQL PATH_LENGTH()
description: Takes a graph path and returns the number of edges in it as INT64, counting edges rather than nodes.

name: GoogleSQL PROPERTY_NAMES()
description: Returns the names of the properties of a graph node or edge as an array of STRING, keeping the original capitalization of each name.

name: GoogleSQL SOURCE_NODE_ID()
description: Takes a graph edge and returns, as a STRING, the unique identifier of the node the edge starts from; the identifier is only meaningful within the query that produced it.

name: CREATE PROPERTY GRAPH
description: Defines a property graph over existing tables, declaring node tables, edge tables with source and destination keys, and the labels and properties that graph queries can match.

name: CREATE OR REPLACE PROPERTY GRAPH
description: Creates a property graph, or replaces the definition of an existing graph with the same name in one statement; it cannot be combined with IF NOT EXISTS.

name: DROP PROPERTY GRAPH
description: Removes a property graph definition from the schema; with IF EXISTS, naming a graph that does not exist is not an error.

name: Graph node-table metadata
description: Schema metadata listing each node table of a property graph with its base table, key columns, labels and properties, read from the JSON column of INFORMATION_SCHEMA.PROPERTY_GRAPHS.

name: Graph edge-table metadata
description: Schema metadata listing each edge table of a property graph with its base table, key columns, labels, properties and the source and destination node tables it connects.

name: Graph label/property metadata
description: Schema metadata naming each label of a property graph with the properties it exposes, plus every property declaration with its name and value type.

name: Graph algorithm PageRank
description: Scores each node by importance, treating a node as more important when many important nodes link to it; takes a damping factor and iteration limit and returns a node and score per row.
notes: Computes local results; methods may be emulator-defined; Google's emulator returns empty results.

name: Graph algorithm BetweennessCentrality
description: Scores how often a node lies on shortest paths between other nodes, so bridge nodes score high; an optional num_source_nodes samples sources instead of using every node.
notes: Computes local results; methods may be emulator-defined; Google's emulator returns empty results.

name: Graph algorithm ClosenessCentrality
description: Scores how close a node is to all other nodes; has an EXACT mode, a sampled HYBRID mode, and an optional Wasserman-Faust normalization for graphs that are not fully connected.
notes: Computes local results; methods may be emulator-defined; Google's emulator returns empty results.

name: Graph algorithm WeaklyConnectedComponents
description: Partitions nodes into disjoint sets in which every node can reach every other node when edge direction is ignored, returning each node with its component number as cluster.
notes: Computes local results; methods may be emulator-defined; Google's emulator returns empty results.

name: Graph algorithm ModularityClustering
description: Partitions the graph into clusters by optimizing modularity, a measure of how dense connections are inside clusters; a resolution parameter tunes granularity and each node gets a cluster number.
notes: Computes local results; methods may be emulator-defined; Google's emulator returns empty results.

name: Graph algorithm CorrelationClustering
description: Groups nodes by pairwise similarity, keeping similar nodes together and dissimilar nodes apart; it requires a resolution parameter and returns each node with its cluster number.
notes: Computes local results; methods may be emulator-defined; Google's emulator returns empty results.

name: Graph algorithm LabelPropagation
description: Assigns clusters by repeatedly letting each node adopt the label held by most of its neighbors, optionally starting from labels stored in a node property, for a limited number of iterations.
notes: Computes local results; methods may be emulator-defined; Google's emulator returns empty results.

name: Graph algorithm CliqueFinding
description: Finds possibly overlapping dense communities so that every clique, a group of nodes all connected to each other, lies in at least one cluster; a node can appear in several rows.
notes: Computes local results; methods may be emulator-defined; Google's emulator returns empty results.

name: Graph algorithm JaccardSimilarity
description: Scores pairs of source and target nodes by the ratio of the neighbors they share to all neighbors either has, returning source node, target node and a similarity value.
notes: Computes local results; methods may be emulator-defined; Google's emulator returns empty results.

name: Graph algorithm CosineSimilarity
description: Scores pairs of source and target nodes from the edge weights toward their common neighbors, returning source node, target node and a similarity value.
notes: Computes local results; methods may be emulator-defined; Google's emulator returns empty results.

name: Graph algorithm CommonNeighborsSimilarity
description: Scores pairs of source and target nodes by the number of neighbors the two nodes have in common, returning source node, target node and a similarity value.
notes: Computes local results; methods may be emulator-defined; Google's emulator returns empty results.

name: Graph algorithm TotalNeighborsSimilarity
description: Scores pairs of source and target nodes by the number of neighbors that at least one of the two nodes has, returning source node, target node and a similarity value.
notes: Computes local results; methods may be emulator-defined; Google's emulator returns empty results.

name: Graph algorithm ShortestPath
description: Finds shortest paths from a set of source nodes to a set of target nodes, returning each pair with the path as a GRAPH_PATH value and its cost.
notes: Computes local results; methods may be emulator-defined; Google's emulator returns empty results.

name: Personalized PageRank
description: PageRank run with source_nodes given, so scores measure importance relative to those starting nodes rather than the whole graph; each row holds a node and its score.
notes: Uses supplied personalization inputs.

name: Graph algorithm CALL PER ()
description: Runs a graph algorithm on the logical subgraph made of the nodes and edges selected by the preceding MATCH rows, unlike a plain CALL, which runs on the whole graph.
notes: Consumes preceding query rows.

name: Graph EXPORT DATA to CLOUD_SPANNER tables
description: Writes algorithm results into an existing table of the same instance, using write_mode update_ignore_all or upsert_ignore_all; rows that violate constraints are skipped.
notes: Writes computed rows; violating rows may be skipped.

name: Graph EXPORT DATA to CSV
description: Writes algorithm results as CSV text to Cloud Storage, with options such as header, field_delimiter, overwrite and GZIP compression; nested and repeated data cannot be exported.
notes: Validates options, then discards rows.

name: Graph EXPORT DATA to Parquet
description: Writes algorithm results to Cloud Storage in the columnar Parquet format, with options overwrite and compression of SNAPPY, GZIP or ZSTD.
notes: Validates options, then discards rows.

name: Graph EXPORT DATA to Avro
description: Writes algorithm results to Cloud Storage in the row-oriented Avro format, with options overwrite and compression of DEFLATE or SNAPPY.
notes: Validates options, then discards rows.

name: CREATE MODEL REMOTE
description: Registers a reference to a model endpoint on Vertex AI as a schema object, with optional INPUT and OUTPUT column lists and an endpoint option; the model itself is not copied into the database.

name: CREATE OR REPLACE MODEL
description: Creates a remote model definition, or replaces an existing one with the same name, for example to point it at a different endpoint or change its input and output columns.

name: ALTER MODEL SET OPTIONS
description: Changes options of an existing model definition, such as endpoint, endpoints for failover, and default_batch_size; setting an option to null restores its default.

name: DROP MODEL
description: Removes a model definition from the database; queries that reference it then fail, while the Vertex AI endpoint itself is unaffected.

name: ML.PREDICT() model inference
description: Table-valued function that runs a registered model over each row of an input table or subquery and returns the model outputs together with the input's pass-through columns.
notes: Production requires model-backed inference; Emulators return placeholders by default.

name: PostgreSQL spanner.ml_predict_row() model inference
description: PostgreSQL-dialect scalar function that sends one row's arguments as JSONB to a Vertex AI endpoint and returns the prediction as JSONB, usable wherever a scalar expression is allowed.
notes: Production requires model-backed inference; Emulators return placeholders by default.

name: AI.IF() model inference
description: Asks a Gemini model whether a natural-language condition in a prompt string is true and returns a BOOL; returns NULL when an argument is NULL or the prompt is empty.
notes: Production requires model-backed inference; Emulators return placeholders by default.

name: AI.SCORE() model inference
description: Rates the input described in a prompt according to a scoring scheme stated in the prompt and returns a FLOAT64, commonly combined with ORDER BY to rank rows.
notes: Production requires model-backed inference; Emulators return placeholders by default.

name: AI.CLASSIFY() model inference
description: Assigns the input prompt to one of the categories you list, either as plain names or as name and description pairs, and returns the best-fitting category as a STRING.
notes: Production requires model-backed inference; Emulators return placeholders by default.

name: Google-hosted Vertex AI endpoint execution
description: Spanner sends model input from a query directly to a model deployed on a Vertex AI endpoint and returns the endpoint's predictions into the query, without a client round trip.
notes: Not called by either local emulator.

name: INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES
description: Lists the tables, views and synonyms of the database with schema, name and type, and for interleaved tables the parent table and ON DELETE action.

name: INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS
description: Lists the columns of every table and view with name, ordinal position, Spanner type, nullability and default, plus flags for generated, hidden and stored columns.

name: INFORMATION_SCHEMA.INDEXES
description: Lists the indexes of the database, including primary keys, with table, name, type, uniqueness, whether NULL entries are filtered, parent table when interleaved, and index state.

name: INFORMATION_SCHEMA.VIEWS
description: Lists the views of the database with their defining SQL text and whether each view runs with invoker rights or definer rights.

name: INFORMATION_SCHEMA.SCHEMATA
description: Lists the schemas of the database, including INFORMATION_SCHEMA and any named schemas, with a PROTO_BUNDLE column that is NULL when the database has no proto bundle.

name: INFORMATION_SCHEMA.SEQUENCES
description: Lists the sequences defined in the database with their catalog, schema, name and value type, which is INT64.

name: INFORMATION_SCHEMA role-based object filtering
description: Limits INFORMATION_SCHEMA rows to objects the current database role holds privileges on; principals with database-level IAM permissions or the spanner_info_reader role see all rows.
notes: Filters metadata by creator_role.

name: SPANNER_SYS.QUERY_STATS_TOP_MINUTE
description: Per-query statistics for the highest-CPU queries in each one-minute interval, grouped by query text or request tag, with execution count, latency, CPU time and rows scanned.
notes: Measured local values or stored metadata; physical fields may be zero.

name: SPANNER_SYS.QUERY_STATS_TOP_10MINUTE
description: Per-query statistics for the highest-CPU queries in each ten-minute interval, with the same columns as the minute table but kept for days rather than hours.
notes: Measured local values or stored metadata; physical fields may be zero.

name: SPANNER_SYS.QUERY_STATS_TOP_HOUR
description: Per-query statistics for the highest-CPU queries in each one-hour interval, retained longest of the three TOP tables, for spotting expensive query patterns over weeks.
notes: Measured local values or stored metadata; physical fields may be zero.

name: SPANNER_SYS.QUERY_STATS_TOTAL_MINUTE
description: One row per one-minute interval combining all queries run on the database, including failed and canceled ones, with total counts, latency and CPU but no query text.
notes: Measured local values or stored metadata; physical fields may be zero.

name: SPANNER_SYS.QUERY_STATS_TOTAL_10MINUTE
description: One row per ten-minute interval combining every query on the database, including those missing from the TOP table, with execution counts, failures, latency and CPU; kept for about four days.
notes: Measured local values or stored metadata; physical fields may be zero.

name: SPANNER_SYS.QUERY_STATS_TOTAL_HOUR
description: One row per one-hour interval combining every query on the database, with execution count, failures, latency and CPU; the longest-retained database-wide query summary.
notes: Measured local values or stored metadata; physical fields may be zero.

name: SPANNER_SYS.READ_STATS_TOP_MINUTE
description: Statistics for the highest-CPU read shapes, meaning sets of columns read, in each one-minute interval, with execution count, average rows, bytes, CPU and locking delay.
notes: Measured local values or stored metadata; physical fields may be zero.

name: SPANNER_SYS.READ_STATS_TOP_10MINUTE
description: Statistics for the highest-CPU read shapes in each ten-minute interval, grouped by columns read or request tag, with READ_TYPE telling plain reads from partitioned reads.
notes: Measured local values or stored metadata; physical fields may be zero.

name: SPANNER_SYS.READ_STATS_TOP_HOUR
description: Statistics for the highest-CPU read shapes in each one-hour interval, kept for about a month, for finding read patterns that drive CPU use over a long period.
notes: Measured local values or stored metadata; physical fields may be zero.

name: SPANNER_SYS.READ_STATS_TOTAL_MINUTE
description: One row per one-minute interval aggregating all reads on the database, including ones the TOP table dropped, with execution count, rows, bytes, CPU, locking delay and client wait.
notes: Measured local values or stored metadata; physical fields may be zero.

name: SPANNER_SYS.READ_STATS_TOTAL_10MINUTE
description: One row per ten-minute interval aggregating every read on the database, with no per-shape columns such as READ_COLUMNS, REQUEST_TAG or READ_TYPE.
notes: Measured local values or stored metadata; physical fields may be zero.

name: SPANNER_SYS.READ_STATS_TOTAL_HOUR
description: One row per one-hour interval aggregating every read on the database, retained longest of the TOTAL read tables, for long-range trends in read volume and CPU.
notes: Measured local values or stored metadata; physical fields may be zero.

name: SPANNER_SYS.TXN_STATS_TOP_MINUTE
description: Statistics for the most resource-consuming transaction shapes in each one-minute interval, identified by FPRINT, with columns read and written, aborts, participants and latencies.
notes: Measured local values or stored metadata; physical fields may be zero.

name: SPANNER_SYS.TXN_STATS_TOP_10MINUTE
description: Statistics for the most resource-consuming transaction shapes in each ten-minute interval, one row per shape, with retry and abort counts, average latencies and bytes written.
notes: Measured local values or stored metadata; physical fields may be zero.

name: SPANNER_SYS.TXN_STATS_TOP_HOUR
description: Statistics for the most resource-consuming transaction shapes in each one-hour interval, kept for about a month, for spotting slow or abort-prone transaction patterns.
notes: Measured local values or stored metadata; physical fields may be zero.

name: SPANNER_SYS.TXN_STATS_TOTAL_MINUTE
description: One row per one-minute interval aggregating every transaction on the database, with attempt, abort and retry counts, participants, latencies and bytes written, but no per-shape columns.
notes: Measured local values or stored metadata; physical fields may be zero.

name: SPANNER_SYS.TXN_STATS_TOTAL_10MINUTE
description: One row per ten-minute interval aggregating every transaction on the database, including transactions absent from the TOP table, with attempt, abort and latency figures; kept for about four days.
notes: Measured local values or stored metadata; physical fields may be zero.

name: SPANNER_SYS.TXN_STATS_TOTAL_HOUR
description: One row per one-hour interval aggregating every transaction on the database, the longest-retained database-wide summary of transaction attempts, aborts and latencies.
notes: Measured local values or stored metadata; physical fields may be zero.

name: SPANNER_SYS.LOCK_STATS_TOP_MINUTE
description: Row key ranges with the highest cumulative lock wait time in each one-minute interval, with the wait in seconds and sampled lock requests naming column, lock mode and transaction tag.
notes: Measured local values or stored metadata; physical fields may be zero.

name: SPANNER_SYS.LOCK_STATS_TOP_10MINUTE
description: Row key ranges with the highest cumulative lock wait time in each ten-minute interval, showing where lock conflicts occurred, with sampled lock requests; kept for days.
notes: Measured local values or stored metadata; physical fields may be zero.

name: SPANNER_SYS.LOCK_STATS_TOP_HOUR
description: Row key ranges with the highest cumulative lock wait time in each one-hour interval, kept for about a month, for tracing recurring hotspots and lock contention.
notes: Measured local values or stored metadata; physical fields may be zero.

name: SPANNER_SYS.LOCK_STATS_TOTAL_MINUTE
description: One row per one-minute interval with TOTAL_LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS, the lock wait time of the whole database, including waits that the TOP table does not list.
notes: Measured local values or stored metadata; physical fields may be zero.

name: SPANNER_SYS.LOCK_STATS_TOTAL_10MINUTE
description: One row per ten-minute interval with the total lock wait time of the whole database in seconds, which can be compared with the waits listed in the TOP rows; kept for several days.
notes: Measured local values or stored metadata; physical fields may be zero.

name: SPANNER_SYS.LOCK_STATS_TOTAL_HOUR
description: One row per one-hour interval with the total lock wait time of the whole database in seconds, kept for about a month to show long-range contention trends.
notes: Measured local values or stored metadata; physical fields may be zero.

name: SPANNER_SYS.TABLE_OPERATIONS_STATS_HOUR
description: Per-table and per-index counts of read queries, writes and deletes in each one-hour interval, counting each operation once whatever the row count; kept for about a month.
notes: Measured local values or stored metadata; physical fields may be zero.

name: SPANNER_SYS.COLUMN_OPERATIONS_STATS_HOUR
description: Per-column counts of reads, queries reading the column and writes in each one-hour interval, plus a flag showing when collection was capped by memory pressure.
notes: Measured local values or stored metadata; physical fields may be zero.

name: SPANNER_SYS.TABLE_SIZES_STATS_1HOUR
description: Size in bytes of each table and index, averaged per clock hour, with total, SSD and HDD bytes; meant for size trends over time, not real-time monitoring.
notes: Measured local values or stored metadata; physical fields may be zero.

name: SPANNER_SYS.OLDEST_ACTIVE_QUERIES
description: Currently running queries sorted from the oldest start time, with query text, session ID and a query ID that CALL cancel_query can use to cancel it; change stream queries are left out.
notes: Measured local values or stored metadata; physical fields may be zero.

name: SPANNER_SYS.ACTIVE_QUERIES_SUMMARY
description: Summary of running queries: the total active count, an upper bound on the oldest start time, and counts of queries older than one, ten and one hundred seconds.
notes: Measured local values or stored metadata; physical fields may be zero.

name: SPANNER_SYS.ACTIVE_PARTITIONED_DMLS
description: Partitioned DML statements currently running, with statement text, session, partitions completed out of total, a progress fraction, rows processed and last update time.
notes: Measured local values or stored metadata; physical fields may be zero.

name: SPANNER_SYS.ROW_DELETION_POLICIES
description: TTL status per table with a row deletion policy: a processed watermark, the count of rows the policy could not delete, and the oldest timestamp among those rows.
notes: Measured local values or stored metadata; physical fields may be zero.

name: SPANNER_SYS.USER_SPLIT_POINTS
description: Lists the user-created split points of a database, which pre-split tables or indexes ahead of expected traffic, with table, index, split key, initiator and expiration time.
notes: Measured local values or stored metadata; physical fields may be zero.

name: SPANNER_SYS.TABLE_OPERATIONS_STATS_MINUTE
description: Per-table and per-index counts of read queries, writes and deletes in each one-minute interval, counting each operation once whatever the row count; kept for about six hours.
notes: Measured local operation counts for the named interval.

name: SPANNER_SYS.TABLE_OPERATIONS_STATS_10MINUTE
description: Per-table and per-index counts of read queries, writes and deletes in each ten-minute interval, counting each operation once whatever the row count; kept for about four days.
notes: Measured local operation counts for the named interval.

name: SPANNER_SYS.COLUMN_OPERATIONS_STATS_MINUTE
description: Per-column counts of reads, queries reading the column and writes in each one-minute interval, the finest-grained column usage view, kept for about six hours.
notes: Measured local operation counts for the named interval.

name: SPANNER_SYS.COLUMN_OPERATIONS_STATS_10MINUTE
description: Per-column counts of reads, queries reading the column and writes in each ten-minute interval, kept for about four days.
notes: Measured local operation counts for the named interval.

name: SPANNER_SYS.SUPPORTED_OPTIMIZER_VERSIONS
description: Lists the query optimizer versions a database can select, with each version's release date and whether it is the current default version.
notes: Static supported-version catalog.

name: INFORMATION_SCHEMA.ROLES
description: Lists the database roles of the database, including system roles, and flags which of them are system roles.
notes: Reports persisted role/grant metadata in the supported local scope.

name: INFORMATION_SCHEMA.ROLE_GRANTEES
description: Lists explicit role memberships, showing which role each grantee belongs to; implicit membership in the public role is left out.
notes: Reports persisted role/grant metadata in the supported local scope.

name: INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLE_PRIVILEGES
description: Lists table-level SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE privileges granted to database roles, including public, with table name and grantee.
notes: Reports persisted role/grant metadata in the supported local scope.

name: INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMN_PRIVILEGES
description: Lists column-level SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE privileges granted to database roles, including public, with table, column, privilege type and grantee.
notes: Reports persisted role/grant metadata in the supported local scope.

name: INFORMATION_SCHEMA.ROUTINE_PRIVILEGES
description: Lists EXECUTE privileges granted on change stream read functions, with the routine name and the grantee.
notes: Reports persisted role/grant metadata in the supported local scope.

name: Typed long-running operation metadata
description: A long-running operation's metadata field holds a message specific to the operation, such as UpdateDatabaseDdlMetadata for schema changes, so clients can read progress details while it runs.
notes: Operations normally complete before the request returns.

name: DatabaseAdminService.ListDatabaseRoles
description: Lists the database roles defined in a database, the named privilege collections used for fine-grained access control.

name: CREATE ROLE
description: Defines a new database role, a named collection of fine-grained access control privileges that can be granted to principals and to other roles.
notes: Role metadata and restricted sessions; no IAM check to select a role.

name: DROP ROLE
description: Removes a database role once all privileges granted to it are revoked; dropping a role also removes its membership in other roles.
notes: Role metadata and restricted sessions; no IAM check to select a role.

name: creator_role session validation
description: The database role named when a session is created, which limits that session's reads, queries and writes to the privileges granted to the role under fine-grained access control.
notes: Role metadata and restricted sessions; no IAM check to select a role.

name: DatabaseAdminService.SetIamPolicy
description: Sets the access control policy on a database or backup, replacing any policy that was already there.
notes: Stores/returns policies; no authenticated IAM enforcement.

name: DatabaseAdminService.GetIamPolicy
description: Returns the access control policy of a database or backup, or an empty policy when none has been set.
notes: Stores/returns policies; no authenticated IAM enforcement.

name: DatabaseAdminService.TestIamPermissions
description: Returns which of a list of permissions the caller holds on a database or backup, so a client can check its access without changing anything.
notes: Returns requested permissions; it does not evaluate IAM access.

name: InstanceAdminService.SetIamPolicy
