description: Sets the access control policy on an instance, replacing any policy that was already there.
notes: Stores/returns policies; no authenticated IAM enforcement.

name: InstanceAdminService.GetIamPolicy
description: Returns the access control policy of an instance, or an empty policy when none has been set.
notes: Stores/returns policies; no authenticated IAM enforcement.

name: InstanceAdminService.TestIamPermissions
description: Returns which of a list of permissions the caller holds on an instance, so a client can check its access without changing anything.
notes: Returns requested permissions; it does not evaluate IAM access.

name: Authenticated IAM authorization decisions
description: Each request is attributed to an authenticated IAM identity and allowed only if its roles grant the needed permission, such as spanner.databases.select, at project, instance or database level.
notes: No authenticated principal reaches the emulator.

name: GRANT SELECT privilege
description: Gives a database role permission to read a table, a view or chosen columns; GoogleSQL ends the statement with TO ROLE name, PostgreSQL with TO name.
notes: Both dialects; sessions without creator_role retain full access.

name: GRANT INSERT privilege
description: Gives a database role permission to add rows to a table, optionally limited to listed columns, so inserts through DML or mutations are allowed for that role.
notes: Both dialects; sessions without creator_role retain full access.

name: GRANT UPDATE privilege
description: Gives a database role permission to change existing rows of a table, optionally limited to listed columns, so updates through DML or mutations are allowed for that role.
notes: Both dialects; sessions without creator_role retain full access.

name: GRANT DELETE privilege
description: Gives a database role permission to delete rows from a table; unlike SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE, this privilege cannot be limited to columns.
notes: Both dialects; sessions without creator_role retain full access.

name: GRANT EXECUTE privilege
description: Gives a database role permission to run a change stream's read function or to call an ML model, for example through ML.PREDICT.
notes: Both dialects; sessions without creator_role retain full access.

name: GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA
description: Gives a database role access to a named, non-default schema; the role needs it in addition to table privileges before it can use objects inside that schema.
notes: Both dialects; sessions without creator_role retain full access.

name: GRANT role membership
description: Makes one database role a member of another so that it inherits the parent role's privileges; GoogleSQL uses GRANT ROLE parent TO ROLE child, PostgreSQL uses GRANT parent TO child.
notes: Both dialects; sessions without creator_role retain full access.

name: REVOKE object privilege
description: Removes privileges such as SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or EXECUTE that were granted on an object, or on chosen columns, from a database role.
notes: Both dialects; sessions without creator_role retain full access.

name: REVOKE role membership
description: Removes a role's membership in another role so it no longer inherits that role's privileges; GoogleSQL uses REVOKE ROLE parent FROM ROLE child, PostgreSQL uses REVOKE parent FROM child.
notes: Both dialects; sessions without creator_role retain full access.

name: Column-level privilege enforcement
description: Lets SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE privileges be granted on chosen columns, so a role can read or change only those columns; DELETE cannot be limited to columns.
notes: Both dialects; sessions without creator_role retain full access.

name: Customer-managed encryption keys
description: Encrypts a database and its backups with a key you own in Cloud KMS instead of the default Google-managed key, so you control the key's rotation, disabling and destruction.
notes: Local data is plaintext; CMEK unavailable.

name: Cloud Audit Logs
description: Records who did what in Spanner as Cloud Audit Logs entries, covering Admin Activity for configuration changes and Data Access for reads and writes.
notes: No production audit logging.

name: Distributed replication
description: Spanner synchronously replicates each split of data across replicas in several zones or regions using Paxos, with a leader ordering writes, so data survives failures.
notes: No distributed local deployment simulation.

name: Multi-region serving
description: A multi-region instance configuration places read-write, read-only and witness replicas in several regions, so data stays readable and writable if a whole region fails.
notes: No distributed local deployment simulation.

name: Physical regional row placement
description: Stores rows in the geographic regions chosen for them, using a placement key column whose value maps each row to a placement in a specific region.
notes: No distributed local deployment simulation.

name: Physical compute autoscaling
description: The managed autoscaler adds or removes an instance's compute capacity in nodes or processing units as CPU load and storage change, within minimum and maximum limits you set.
notes: Capacity is local metadata.

name: Cloud Monitoring integration
description: Publishes Spanner instance and database metrics such as CPU utilization, storage use and request latency to Cloud Monitoring for dashboards, charts and alerting policies.
notes: Not emulated.

name: Table-count limit validation
description: Enforces the maximum number of tables allowed in one database, rejecting a schema change that would create more tables than the limit.
notes: Selected API/schema limits only, not all cloud quotas.

name: Index-count limit validation
description: Enforces the maximum number of indexes allowed per database and per table, rejecting a schema change that would go over either limit.
notes: Selected API/schema limits only, not all cloud quotas.

name: Mutation-count validation
description: Caps the number of mutations one transaction may send, counted per modified column and per affected index entry, and rejects a transaction that goes over the cap.
notes: Selected API/schema limits only, not all cloud quotas.

name: Value-size validation
description: Caps the size of a single cell value, such as a STRING or BYTES value, and rejects a write whose value is larger than the cap.
notes: Selected API/schema limits only, not all cloud quotas.

name: Admin API rate quotas
description: Limits how many instance, database and backup admin API requests a project or user may send per period, including polling of long-running operations; extra requests are rejected.
notes: Not enforced locally.

name: Capacity-based admission quotas
description: Quotas bound how much compute capacity a project may provision per region, and an instance accepts only the load its provisioned capacity can serve.
notes: Not enforced locally.

name: default_leader physical routing effect
description: Names the read-write region that hosts leader replicas for a dual-region or multi-region database, so writes are first handled in that region, close to the writers.
notes: Stored metadata does not select a real regional leader.

name: Spanner gRPC endpoint
description: The data API endpoint where clients call the Spanner service over gRPC to create sessions and run reads, queries and transactions against a database.

name: Spanner REST gateway
description: An HTTP and JSON interface to the same data API, exposing session, query, read and transaction methods as resource-style REST calls.

name: Google JSON REST error envelope
description: The format of REST error responses: a JSON error object with an HTTP code, a message, a canonical status name such as NOT_FOUND, and a details array of typed information.
notes: Preserves HTTP status, canonical name and standard details.

name: Python Spanner client
description: Google Cloud client library for Python, with Client, Instance and Database objects, snapshots for reads and run_in_transaction for read-write work.
notes: Connects through SPANNER_EMULATOR_HOST.

name: Go Spanner client
description: Google Cloud client library for Go, built around a Client that offers single reads, read-only transactions and ReadWriteTransaction, which retries aborted transactions.
notes: Connects through SPANNER_EMULATOR_HOST.

name: Node.js Spanner client
description: Google Cloud client library for Node.js, with Spanner, Instance, Database and Table classes whose methods return promises, for reads, queries and transactions.
notes: Connects through SPANNER_EMULATOR_HOST.

name: Java Spanner client
description: Google Cloud client library for Java, built around a DatabaseClient that offers reads, queries, mutations and transaction runners, with synchronous and asynchronous APIs.
notes: Connects through SPANNER_EMULATOR_HOST.

name: C++ Spanner client
description: Google Cloud client library for C++, built around a Client class whose operations return StatusOr results, with typed Value objects for parameters and rows.
notes: Connects through SPANNER_EMULATOR_HOST.

name: Spanner JDBC driver
description: Java driver that lets applications use Spanner through standard JDBC Connection, Statement and ResultSet interfaces, for GoogleSQL databases and PostgreSQL-dialect databases.
notes: PostgreSQL wire clients require PGAdapter.

name: PGAdapter with pgJDBC
description: Lets the standard PostgreSQL JDBC driver, pgJDBC, reach a PostgreSQL-dialect database through PGAdapter, which translates PostgreSQL wire protocol messages into Spanner gRPC calls.
notes: PostgreSQL wire clients require PGAdapter.

name: PGAdapter with psql
description: Lets the standard PostgreSQL command-line client, psql, connect to PGAdapter's PostgreSQL wire protocol endpoint and run interactive SQL against a PostgreSQL-dialect database.
notes: PostgreSQL wire clients require PGAdapter.

name: Committed row persistence
description: Rows written by a finished read-write transaction are stored durably on multiple replicas, so later strong reads return them even after server failures or maintenance.
notes: Requires --data_dir; local LevelDB row writes are not synced against host power loss, unlike the production durability contract.

name: Schema DDL persistence
description: Schema changes such as new tables, columns and indexes are stored durably as part of the database, so the schema remains the same across failures and maintenance.
notes: Requires --data_dir; power-loss durability and type limitations remain documented.

name: Instance metadata persistence
description: An instance's configuration, display name, labels and compute capacity are stored durably by the Spanner control plane and stay readable until the instance is deleted.
notes: Requires --data_dir; power-loss durability and type limitations remain documented.

name: Database metadata persistence
description: A database's name, state, dialect, options and encryption settings are stored durably and stay readable through the admin API until the database is dropped.
notes: Requires --data_dir; power-loss durability and type limitations remain documented.

name: Instance partition persistence
description: Instance partitions, the regional compute and storage units that hold the geo-partitioned data of an instance, are stored durably and stay listable until deleted.
notes: Requires --data_dir; power-loss durability and type limitations remain documented.

name: IAM policy persistence
description: IAM policies set on instances and databases are stored durably, so the same roles keep granting access to the same principals until the policy is changed.
notes: Requires --data_dir; power-loss durability and type limitations remain documented.

name: Long-running operation persistence
description: Long-running operations such as database creation are recorded durably, so a client can fetch their status and result by operation name even after the work has finished.
notes: Requires --data_dir; power-loss durability and type limitations remain documented.

name: Backup metadata persistence
description: A backup's name, source database, creation time, expiry time and state are stored durably and stay readable until the backup is deleted or expires.
notes: Requires --data_dir; power-loss durability and type limitations remain documented.

name: Backup schedule persistence
description: A backup schedule's settings, such as its frequency, retention duration and encryption configuration, are stored durably, so scheduled backups keep being created.
notes: Requires --data_dir; power-loss durability and type limitations remain documented.

name: Change-stream record persistence
description: Data change records produced by a change stream are stored durably for the stream's retention period, so readers can read them again from any point within that period.
notes: Requires --data_dir; power-loss durability and type limitations remain documented.

name: Change-stream partition-history persistence
description: Partition metadata of a change stream, recording how partitions split and merge over time, is stored durably so readers can follow child partitions without losing records.
notes: Requires --data_dir; power-loss durability and type limitations remain documented.

name: SPANNER_SYS interval persistence
description: Statistics gathered into SPANNER_SYS tables stay queryable for a minimum period after each interval ends, so past minute, ten-minute and hour windows can still be read.
notes: Requires --data_dir; power-loss durability and type limitations remain documented.

name: Persistent TOKENLIST values
description: TOKENLIST values, the tokenized form of text that full-text search indexes use, are generated from their source column and stored durably with the row.
notes: Requires --data_dir; power-loss durability and type limitations remain documented.

name: Persistent PostgreSQL NUMERIC values
description: PostgreSQL-dialect NUMERIC values keep their exact decimal digits, including NaN, when they are stored durably and are read back unchanged.
notes: Requires --data_dir; power-loss durability and type limitations remain documented.

name: Persistent PostgreSQL JSONB values
description: PostgreSQL-dialect JSONB values are stored durably in their normalized form, and reading them back returns the same JSON content.
notes: Requires --data_dir; power-loss durability and type limitations remain documented.

name: Persistent non-NULL PROTO values
description: Non-NULL PROTO column values, serialized protocol buffer messages, are stored durably with the row and are read back as the same message.
notes: Value codec returns UNIMPLEMENTED; no commit is stored.

name: Persistent non-NULL ENUM values
description: Non-NULL ENUM column values, named integer constants from a protocol buffer enum in the schema's proto bundle, are stored durably and read back unchanged.
notes: Value codec returns UNIMPLEMENTED; no commit is stored.
